findings.title: `ensurePacks` blocks the event loop — the "resolves alongside gather" concurrency is not real
findings.body:
Rule violated (skill: *Always use Node.js async functions ... to avoid blocking the event loop*, and *use `async/await` for asynchronous code*): `ensurePacks` is a fully synchronous function — every git call in `src/packs/sync.ts` goes through `execFileSync('git', ...)` with a 5-minute per-invocation timeout. Wrapping it in `Promise.resolve().then(...)` does not make it concurrent: it only defers the body to the next microtask checkpoint, where it then blocks the event loop for the entire duration of every clone.

So the comment above this line ("Packs + Linguist resolve alongside gather/companion detection") does not hold. On a first review the three default packs (`awesome-copilot`, `CheatSheetSeries`, `Anthropic-Cybersecurity-Skills`) clone one after another, each up to `GIT_TIMEOUT_MS` (5 min), and during that window no JS continuation can run — the in-flight gather response, the Linguist fetch, and the companion-detection child-process callbacks are all parked until the last clone returns. Nothing else in the process can make progress either (no progress append, no queued signal handling).

Fix: make the git seam async and `await` it. Change `GitExec` to return `Promise<string>` backed by `promisify(execFile)` from `node:child_process` (same `cwd`/`timeout`/`env` options), make `ensurePacks` (and `syncPacks`) `async`, and drop the `Promise.resolve().then(...)` wrapper here in favour of calling `ensurePacks(...)` directly so the returned promise is genuinely pending while gather runs. If per-pack clones should also overlap each other, replace the sequential `for` loop with `Promise.all` over the packs (the existing `p-limit` dependency can cap concurrency). Keeping the synchronous version is also fine — but then the comment should say the clones are blocking, rather than claiming parallelism the code does not provide.

findings.title: Hand-rolled file-URL→path conversion breaks on paths containing spaces
findings.body:
`ROOT` converts `import.meta.url` to a filesystem path by hand:

```js
const ROOT = resolve(new URL('..', import.meta.url).pathname.replace(/^\/([A-Za-z]:)/, '$1'));
```

`URL.pathname` is percent-encoded, so a checkout under a path with a space (very common on Windows: `C:\Users\John Doe\repos\pr-review`) yields `C:\Users\John%20Doe\repos\pr-review`. `CLI` and `FIXTURES` then point at a non-existent directory and the harness dies with the misleading `dist/cli.cjs not found — run \`npm run build\` first.` even after a successful build. Verified: `new URL('..', 'file:///C:/Users/John%20Doe/.../scripts/eval.mjs')` → hand-rolled `C:\Users\John%20Doe\...` vs `fileURLToPath` → `C:\Users\John Doe\...`.

Rule violated: "Use Node.js built-in modules and avoid external dependencies where possible" / "Keep the code simple and maintainable" — Node has this built in.

Fix:
```js
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
const ROOT = resolve(fileURLToPath(new URL('..', import.meta.url)));
```
This also drops the Windows drive-letter regex entirely and works unchanged on POSIX.

findings.title: `Promise.resolve().then(ensurePacks)` fakes concurrency around a fully synchronous git clone
findings.body:
```js
const packsPromise = Promise.resolve().then(() => ensurePacks(config.skillPacks, { home: opts.homeOverride }));
```

`ensurePacks` (`src/packs/sync.ts`) is entirely synchronous — it drives `execFileSync('git', ['clone', ...])` with a 5-minute timeout per pack. Wrapping a blocking call in `Promise.resolve().then()` does not move it off the main thread: the callback runs on the microtask queue at the first `await` (the `await runGather(...)` a few lines down), and blocks the event loop for the whole clone.

So the comment directly above — "Packs + Linguist resolve alongside gather/companion detection" — is not what happens. On a cold machine the three default packs (604/120/489 skills) clone *before* gather's first HTTP request is even issued, and the in-flight `linguistPromise` fetch and the `companionPromise` child process cannot progress meanwhile. Worst case the process is frozen for 3 × 5 min with no output and no signal handling.

Rule violated: "Always use async/await for asynchronous code, and use 'node:util' promisify function to avoid callbacks."

Fix: make the pack path genuinely async — switch `defaultGit` in `src/packs/sync.ts` to `promisify(execFile)` from `node:util`/`node:child_process`, make `GitExec`/`ensurePacks`/`syncPacks` return promises, and `await` them in the existing `Promise.all`. If keeping it sync is deliberate, then call `ensurePacks(...)` directly at that line and correct the comment, so the code does not claim parallelism it does not have.

findings.title: `readdirSync(FIXTURES)` returns files too — one stray file kills the whole eval run
findings.body:
```js
const cases = caseName ? [caseName] : readdirSync(FIXTURES);
```

`readdirSync` without `withFileTypes` lists regular files as well as directories. A `README.md`, `.DS_Store`, or `.gitkeep` dropped into `evals/fixtures/` becomes a "case"; `runCase` then hits `readFileSync(join(dir, 'diff.patch'))` with no try/catch and throws an uncaught ENOENT, aborting every remaining case instead of reporting one failure.

Rule violated: "Ensure tests cover edge cases and error handling" — a harness that crashes on an unexpected directory entry reports nothing about the cases that would have passed.

Fix:
```js
const cases = caseName
  ? [caseName]
  : readdirSync(FIXTURES, { withFileTypes: true }).filter((e) => e.isDirectory()).map((e) => e.name);
```
and wrap the `runCase(c, extra)` call in a try/catch that logs `✗ ${c}: ${err.message}` and counts a failure, so a broken fixture degrades to one failed case.

findings.title: Duplicate `node:fs` import statement
`<comment summary>` is parsed as a raw HTML tag and disappears when rendered
findings.body:
CommonMark **Raw HTML** rule: `<` + a tag name (ASCII letter followed by letters/digits/hyphens) + whitespace-separated attribute names + `>` is a valid open tag and is passed through as literal HTML, so a renderer swallows it. `<comment summary>` matches exactly — tag name `comment`, attribute `summary` — so the placeholder vanishes from the rendered line, leaving `'' — a correção vai …`.

(The sibling placeholder `<concrete visible change, e.g. '…'>` is safe: the comma after `change` is illegal in an attribute name, so it falls back to literal text.)

Fix: wrap the placeholder in a code span like the neighbouring `` `path:line` `` and `` `Visual N` ``, or backslash-escape the angle bracket:

```
… question text = "@reviewer em `path:line`: '`<comment summary>`' — a correção vai …
```

findings.title: Single ~300-word paragraph packs eight distinct rules (plain language)
findings.body:
**Rule (Markdown Accessibility §4 — Plain Language):** "Flag long, dense paragraphs that could be broken into smaller sections or lists."

This one paragraph carries eight separate rules — context-vs-lens split, the glob caveat, the tag rule, the cap of 6, baselines, `skill_packs: []` fallback, index overflow, Linguist stack detection, manifest parsing, ecosystem tags, docs-only triage, and the zero-pass exit code — in ~300 words with no structural break. Screen reader users cannot skim it (there is no heading or list boundary to jump between); readers with cognitive disabilities and non-native speakers have to hold every clause in working memory to reach the rule they came for. Two clauses also use a hyphen where the sentence needs an em dash ("stack hits - `applies_to`/`applyTo` globs …" and "… stack-tag matches - capped at 6"), which reads as a subtraction rather than an aside.

**Suggested fix (author's call on wording):** split into a short lead sentence plus a bulleted list, e.g.

```markdown
Your own skills are CONTEXT, not lenses — every matched repo/forced skill is injected into every pass as authoritative project rules, and never consumes a pass slot. The passes come from the packs:

- **Stack hits** — `applies_to`/`applyTo` globs matching changed files (a bare extension wildcard like `**/*.ts` counts only when the skill's name/tags also overlap the stack), plus exact stack-tag matches. Capped at 6.
- **Every baseline pointer** — the generic security/quality/performance/testing lenses always run.
- **Everything else** — overflow, unmatched skills, and index-mode packs go to `skills-index.md`, which every pass can read on demand.

With `skill_packs: []`, your skills become the passes themselves.
```

Move the stack-detection mechanics (Linguist, manifests, ecosystem tags) and the docs-only/zero-pass behaviour into their own short paragraphs after the list.

findings.title: Bold text used as a heading for the two scope modes
findings.body:
**Rule (Markdown Accessibility §3 — Heading Hierarchy):** "Flag bold text (`**text**`) used as a visual substitute for a proper heading."

`**Full PR mode**` (line 30) and `**Focused mode**` (line 32) each introduce a self-contained block describing one mode — the section exists to distinguish them. Bold gets the visual separation but produces no document structure: assistive technology users navigating by heading (rotor / heading list) jump straight from `## Scope contract` to `## Language rules` and never see that two modes exist, and the modes are absent from any generated table of contents. Screen readers also frequently do not announce bold at all, so the only cue that a new mode has started disappears entirely.

**Fix:** promote both to real H3 headings under `## Scope contract`:

```markdown
### Full PR mode

`/fix <PR_URL>` or `/fix <NUMBER>` — the user has authorized processing **every** review comment. …

### Focused mode

URL contains `#discussion_r<ID>` or `#pullrequestreview-<ID>` — gather auto-detects it …
```

This keeps the visual weight while adding the navigable structure. (Inline bold that leads a sentence, such as `**Pipeline trace (MANDATORY for High risk):**`, is fine — this finding is only about the two mode blocks.)

findings.title: Changelog entry buries a rule in three levels of nested parentheses
findings.body:
**Rule (Markdown Accessibility §4 — Plain Language):** "Favor short sentences, common words, and active voice" / "Flag unnecessarily complex or jargon-heavy language that could be simplified."

The "Historical note" sentence in this bullet runs ~90 words through three levels of nested parentheses:

> an earlier ranked-tier draft (forced > repo (your own skills — `applies_to`-targeted, or untargeted ones promoted by the old name/description relevance heuristic) > pack glob (`applies_to`/`applyTo` vs changed files; a lone `'**'` never counts, and a bare extension wildcard like `**/*.ts` only counts when the skill's name/tags overlap the stack — pack authors use those promiscuously) > pack tag > baseline, single cap 10) was replaced by the context/lenses split above after live testing.

Spoken aloud, nesting is unrecoverable: a screen reader gives no depth cue, so by the time "> pack tag > baseline, single cap 10) was replaced" arrives the listener has lost which clause the subject belonged to. The `>` characters inside prose compound this — they are read as "greater than" and are easy to confuse with blockquote markup.

**Suggested fix (author's call):** this is a historical note about a design that was replaced, so it does not need the full tier detail. Either cut it to one sentence — "An earlier ranked-tier draft (a single cap of 10 across forced / repo / pack-glob / pack-tag / baseline tiers) was replaced by the context-vs-lenses split above after live testing." — or, if the detail matters, lift the tier list out as a nested bullet list under the note.

findings.title: ALL-CAPS carries the emphasis four times in one paragraph
findings.body:
**Rule (Markdown Accessibility §7 — Other):** "Screen readers often don't announce bold or italic emphasis, so critical information should not rely on this styling alone" (the same applies to typographic shouting), and §4 — Plain Language.

This paragraph leans on capitalisation for all of its emphasis: LENSES, CONTEXT (twice), EVERY, PASSES. Capitalisation is a visual-only signal — some screen reader / verbosity configurations spell short all-caps tokens letter by letter, and none of them convey "this word is the important one", so the distinction the sentence is built on (yours = context, packs = lenses) does not survive being read aloud. The contrast is also carried purely by capitalisation rather than by sentence structure. Line 25 additionally uses a hyphen where an em dash is intended ("(`skills-project.md`) - they override generic judgement"), which reads as a stray subtraction.

**Suggested fix (author's call on wording):** state the contrast in the sentence structure and drop the shouting, e.g. "Selection separates lenses from context. Your own skills — repo dirs and forced dirs — are context: every matched one is injected into every pass as an authoritative project rule (`skills-project.md`). They override generic judgement and never consume pass slots. The passes themselves come from the packs: stack hits (glob/tag, capped at `MAX_STACK_PASSES = 6`) plus every baseline pointer, so the generic lenses always run on a code PR." Reserve `**bold**` for the two key terms if visual weight is still wanted.

findings.title: `✅/❌` names a doc format using emoji alone
findings.body:
**Rule (Markdown Accessibility §5 — Emoji):** "Flag multiple consecutive emoji, which are disruptive to screen reader users since each emoji name is read aloud in full" and "Flag emoji used to convey meaning that is not also communicated in text."

"using the ✅/❌ dev-checklist format" is read aloud as "white heavy check mark slash cross mark dev-checklist format" — the two emoji are the entire name of the convention, with no text equivalent anywhere in the sentence, so a listener gets emoji names where they needed a format name.

**Fix:** name the convention in words and keep the emoji as an illustration rather than the label — e.g. "using the dev-checklist's do/don't format (✅ correct example, ❌ wrong example), one code-example pair, ending with 'Found in PR #N.'" The related mention on line 183 ("A bullet like \"✅ original fix preserved\" is a hypothesis, not a trace") is fine as-is: it is quoting a literal bullet, and the surrounding text carries the meaning.

findings.title: New `/fix` command is another project's file — every path it drives resolves to nothing in this repo
findings.body:
`.claude/commands/fix.md` is added verbatim from a different project, so the workflow it documents cannot run here. Step 0 derives `ROOT="$(pwd | grep -o '.*PrecoPratico')"` (empty in this repo) and then `CLI_DIR="$ROOT/PrecoPratico-Docs/tools/cli"`, so `test -f "$CLI"` fails and the `cd "$CLI_DIR"` fallback errors on the very first step. The same holds for every other resource it tells the agent to read or edit: `tools/cli/src/*` (line 25), `.claude/skills/dev-workflow/dev-checklist.md` and `backend-guide/create-services.md` (line 149), `PrecoPratico-Docs/.claude/skills/...` targets (line 212), and `.claude/commands/audit-fixes.md` (line 244) — none of these exist in `pr-review` — plus repo-specific content that has no meaning here (NestJS `@Body`/`@FilesPipeline` pipeline rules at line 126, Backend/Frontend/Types repo selection at line 62).

Markdown content rule 4 requires references to be valid and accessible; a command doc whose every reference dangles is not usable content. Fix: port it before committing it — point Step 0 at this repo's own tooling, drop the PrecoPratico-specific classification, lesson-extraction targets, and framework rules, and remove the links to commands/guides that don't exist here — or leave the file out of this plugin's `.claude/commands/`.

findings.title: `add-pack` skill contradicts itself on when baseline passes dispatch
findings.body:
Step 4 states "Baseline skills dispatch when no glob/tag/repo/forced match fires", but the Rules section 15 lines below (line 47) states the opposite: "passes = pack glob/tag (cap `MAX_STACK_PASSES` = 6; ...) + every baseline". `src/dispatch/pass-select.ts` settles it — `// Baselines ALWAYS dispatch (deduped against a baseline that already ...)` — so line 32 is the pre-0.7 semantics left behind.

This matters more than usual for this file: it is a repo skill, injected into every review pass as authoritative project context, so a reader (human or agent) gets two mutually exclusive rules from one document. Fix: reword line 32 to "Baseline skills dispatch on every code PR, on top of the stack passes (only docs-only PRs skip them)", keeping the pointers-not-content sentence as is.

findings.title: Pack table column header contradicts the baseline behavior described six lines later
findings.body:
The fourth column reads "Baseline passes (run when nothing better matches)", but line 144 of the same section says "plus EVERY baseline pointer (the generic security/quality/performance/testing lenses always run)", and `src/dispatch/pass-select.ts` dispatches baselines unconditionally on a code PR. The parenthetical describes the pre-0.7 fallback semantics that this PR removed, and it sits in the README section whose whole point is explaining the new model — a reader hits the wrong rule first.

Fix: change the header to `Baseline passes (always run on a code PR)`.

findings.title: Relative link to `src/dispatch/parsers.ts` is off by one directory level
findings.body:
Markdown content rule 4: links must be valid and accessible. This line was rewritten in this PR but kept a target that does not resolve — from `skills/help/reference/`, `../../src/dispatch/parsers.ts` points at `skills/src/dispatch/parsers.ts`, which does not exist; reaching the repo root from this directory needs three levels.

Fix: `[src/dispatch/parsers.ts](../../../src/dispatch/parsers.ts)`.

findings.title: Relative link to `README.md` is off by one directory level
findings.body:
Markdown content rule 4: links must be valid and accessible. The rewrite correctly dropped the now-dead `#managing-reviewers` anchor but kept the broken path — from `skills/help/reference/`, `../../README.md` resolves to `skills/README.md`, which does not exist.

Fix: `[README.md](../../../README.md)`.

findings.title: Single ~1,500-character paragraph packs the whole execution model into one line
findings.body:
Markdown content rule 7 caps line length at 400 characters; this rewritten line is roughly 1,500 and runs about a dozen distinct facts (runtime selection, tool vocabulary, pass naming, docs-only triage, parallel dispatch, the untrusted-comment fence, the verifier condition, the exit-2 rule) together with no break. It is the hardest paragraph to scan in the whole help set.

Fix: split it into three or four paragraphs along its natural seams — dispatch mechanics / what a pass is / verifier + exit behavior. Same treatment would help `README.md:144` (~1,370 chars) and `CHANGELOG.md:27` and `:30` (~1,000 chars each), the other worst offenders this PR adds.

findings.title: `<comment summary>` is parsed as raw HTML and disappears from the rendered file
findings.body:
**Rule violated (GFM — Raw HTML / inline):** an inline open tag is `<` + tag name + zero or more attributes + `>`. In `'<comment summary>'` the token `comment` is a valid tag name and `summary` is a valid boolean attribute, so GFM treats `<comment summary>` as raw HTML and passes it through — GitHub's sanitizer then strips the unknown tag. The rendered line reads `question text = "@reviewer em path:line: '' — a correção vai ..."`, silently losing the placeholder that tells the reader what to put there.

Every other placeholder in this file is already wrapped in a code span (e.g. `` `<short title> — <path>:<line>` ``, `` `#discussion_r<ID>` ``), so this line is the odd one out.

**Fix:** wrap the placeholder in a code span (or backslash-escape the `<`):

```
... question text = "@reviewer em `path:line`: '`<comment summary>`' — a correção vai `<concrete visible change, e.g. 'mudar o tab desabilitado de 75/25 para 50/50'>`. Aplicar?"; options:
```

(The second placeholder, `<concrete visible change, …>`, survives by accident — the comma makes `change,` an invalid attribute name so the tag parse fails — but wrapping both keeps the file consistent and immune to a later edit that drops the comma.)

findings.title: A baseline skill that also stack-matches can be silently evicted by MAX_STACK_PASSES
findings.body:
**Correctness — the "baselines ALWAYS dispatch" invariant does not hold.**

In the `packSkills` loop the baseline check is the *last* branch: a skill listed in `baseline:` that also has a glob or tag hit is classified `glob`/`tag`, not `baseline`. It then competes in `stackCandidates`, and if it ranks outside `MAX_STACK_PASSES` it lands in `stackOverflow` → `indexEntries`. The `baselines` filter here only picks `matchedBy === 'baseline'`, so it never gets re-added, and `missingBaseline` does not fire either (the skill *loaded*, it just was not dispatched). The loss is completely silent.

**Verified** against the real `selectPasses` (6 specific-glob pack skills + a baseline that tag-matches):
```
passes: p/spec1..p/spec6 (all glob)
baseline dispatched? false
in index? true
missingBaseline: []
```

**Why this matters:** the cap exists precisely so security/error-handling lenses cannot be starved out (the comment on `MAX_STACK_PASSES` cites the live incident). This path reintroduces exactly that failure, and a user-configured pack whose `baseline:` names a stack-flavoured skill (`typescript-review`, `node-security`, …) hits it on the first PR.

**Suggested fix** — treat baseline membership as an override rather than a fallthrough. Either tag the candidate as baseline up front:
```ts
if (baselineSet.has(s.name)) { candidates.push(candidate(s, 'baseline', tagHits)); continue; }
// …then the glob/tag branches
```
or keep the tier label and re-add evicted baselines after the slice:
```ts
const keptNames = new Set(stackKept.map((c) => c.pass.name));
const baselines = candidates.filter(
  (c) => baselineSet.has(c.pass.name) && !keptNames.has(c.pass.name),
);
const stackOverflow = stackCandidates.slice(MAX_STACK_PASSES).filter((c) => !baselineSet.has(c.pass.name));
```

**Test gap:** `tests/pass-select.test.ts` covers a baseline that stack-matches *inside* the cap ("baseline dedupe keeps the higher tier") and pure baselines riding over a full cap, but not a baseline that stack-matches and ranks past the cap — add that case.

findings.title: `.claude/commands/fix.md` is another project's command — broken in every step in this repo
findings.body:
**Unrelated file committed; every path it depends on is missing here.**

This 265-line command is written for the PrecoPratico workspace, not pr-review. Verified in the checkout:

| Reference | Exists in this repo |
|---|---|
| `PrecoPratico-Docs/tools/cli/dist/fix.js` (the CLI it drives) | no |
| `.claude/commands/audit-fixes.md` (Step 9) | no |
| `.claude/skills/dev-workflow/dev-checklist.md` (Step 4.4) | no |
| `backend-guide/*`, `frontend-guide/*`, `pp-*/SKILL.md` (Step 8 targets) | no |
| `npm run emit` (Step 6) | not in `package.json` scripts (`build build:watch bundle test clean prepare`) |

Step 0 is dead on arrival: `ROOT="$(pwd | grep -o '.*PrecoPratico')"` yields the empty string in `…/repos/pr-review`, so `CLI_DIR="/PrecoPratico-Docs/tools/cli"` and the `npm install && npm run build` fallback runs against a non-existent directory. It also hardcodes NestJS/React/Tailwind/Portuguese specifics and internal PR numbers into a repo whose stated rule is that stack knowledge lives in packs, never in this repo.

The file is not mentioned in AGENTS.md, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, or the PR description, and nothing references it — it reads as an accidental commit of a personal command. But it *is* live: Claude Code registers it, so `/fix` in this repo fails at Step 0.

**Suggested fix:** delete `.claude/commands/fix.md` from this PR. If a `/fix` flow is genuinely wanted here, add it in its own PR, rewritten against this repo's CLI and paths, and documented in AGENTS.md.

findings.title: `syncPacks` leaves a half-cloned pack dir behind, permanently wedging that pack
`skills-all.md` is written every run but never referenced once any project skill matches
findings.body:
**Behavior contradicts the contract this PR documents.**

`authoritativeSkills = ctx.skillsFiles['project'] ?? unionSkills` makes the union file a *fallback*, and the same precedence is used for the Codex sibling (`src/commands/review.ts:770`). Whenever `skills-project.md` exists — the normal case for any repo with skills — `skills-all.md` is referenced by nobody: the companions (line 549), the verifier (line 616), and codex all receive only the project rules.

Confirmed on this PR's own run: `skills-all.md` was written at 71 KB and `grep -c skills-all.md orchestrator-prompt.md` → **0**, against 20 hits for `skills-project.md`.

Two problems:
1. **Doc drift.** `AGENTS.md`, changed in this PR, states `skills-all.md` is the "union read by codex/companions/verifier", and `.claude/skills/debug-review-run.md` repeats it in the artifacts table. Both are wrong as written.
2. **Lost knowledge.** The premise of this PR is that review knowledge lives in the packs. The verifier — whose job is spotting what the passes collectively missed — and the Codex second opinion get zero pack content and must reconcile against lenses they never saw.

There is also a wording bug: `skillsRulesSentence` renders "read the **project-specific rules** at `…`", so on the fallback branch the union pack file is announced to the agent as the project's own authoritative rules.

**Suggested fix:** pass both files rather than choosing one — give the prompt the project rules *and* the union (`skillsRulesSentence(project)` + a separate "reference skills" sentence for `skills-all.md`). If the current precedence is deliberate, stop writing `skills-all.md` when a project file exists and correct the AGENTS.md / debug-review-run.md descriptions in this PR.

findings.title: eval.mjs resolves ROOT from a URL pathname — breaks on any path with a space
findings.body:
**Rung 3 of the ladder: the stdlib already does this.**

`new URL(...).pathname` is percent-encoded, so a checkout under `C:\Users\John Doe\repos\pr-review` yields `.../John%20Doe/...`. The hand-rolled drive-letter regex does not decode it, so `ROOT` points at a directory that does not exist and the harness dies with the misleading `dist/cli.cjs not found — run \`npm run build\` first.` — sending the user to rebuild a bundle that is already there. Same for any non-ASCII path segment.

**Suggested fix:**
```js
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
const ROOT = resolve(fileURLToPath(new URL('..', import.meta.url)));
```
`fileURLToPath` handles the decoding and the Windows drive letter, and the regex goes away.

While in the file: `readdirSync(FIXTURES)` at line 125 also returns plain files, so a stray `README.md` under `evals/fixtures/` makes `runCase` throw out of the loop instead of counting a failure — `readdirSync(FIXTURES, { withFileTypes: true }).filter((e) => e.isDirectory()).map((e) => e.name)` fixes it.

findings.title: Eval case with no `must_find` patterns passes vacuously
Stack-agnostic guard test depends on `process.cwd()` in a file that chdir's
`must_find` regex is loose enough to pass on an unrelated finding
findings.body:
QA Assertion rule violated — *"Always assert the exact expected value, not just truthiness"* / *"Use specific matchers"*.

The alternation's weakest branch is the bare word `batch`, and `scripts/eval.mjs` matches it case-insensitively against `title\n body` of **every** finding in `finalFindings` — this fixture sets no `pass:`, so all ~9 dispatched passes plus codex and the verifier are in scope. "…consider batching these calls", "batch size", or any prose containing `batch` from an unrelated pass satisfies the assertion, and the harness reports the N+1 case green without the planted per-iteration query ever being found. The same shape applies to `inside (the|a) loop`. Nothing checks that the matching finding even points at `src/reports/summary.js`.

Fix — scope the assertion and drop the ambiguous branch:

```yaml
must_find:
  - "N\\+1|per[- ]iteration|one query per (account|id|row|iteration)"
```

and, if a specific lens should own it, add `pass: performance-optimization` so `expected.pass` narrows `inScope` instead of leaving it as the whole run.

findings.title: `packs suggest <pr-url>` logic is untested and unreachable from tests
`TEST_HOME` temp dir is created but never removed
findings.body:
QA Test Data Management rule violated — *"Reset or isolate state between tests"*: every other temp dir in this file is removed in a `finally` (`rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true })`), but this module-level `mkdtempSync` has no counterpart, so each run of `tests/resume.test.ts` leaves a `pr-resume-home-*` directory behind in the OS temp dir forever. On a dev machine or CI runner that runs the suite repeatedly this accumulates unbounded, and it is the only unswept artifact in the file.

Fix — sweep it once when the file's tests are done:

```ts
const TEST_HOME = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'pr-resume-home-'));
process.on('exit', () => rmSync(TEST_HOME, { recursive: true, force: true }));
```

(or wrap the file's tests in a `describe` with an `after()` hook that removes it).

findings.title: `tmpFile()` leaks a temp dir per call and re-creates an existing dir
Pack-sync suite skips itself using the function it is testing
Eval harness crashes instead of reporting a failed case
Repo-controlled `.pr-review.yaml` can point `skill_packs` at any git repo, which is auto-cloned and injected as authoritative agent instructions
findings.body:
OWASP A03 (Software Supply Chain Failures) / A08 (Data Integrity) — and AI1 (prompt injection via untrusted input).

`loadConfig({ cwd })` applies the repo-level `.pr-review.yaml` (`src/config.ts:191`), and `skill_packs` uses REPLACE semantics, so a repo yaml overrides the global/default pack list entirely. This line then clones every entry with no confirmation, and `loadPackSkills` turns that third-party markdown into `pass-*.md` bodies dispatched to `general-purpose` agents in a runtime spawned with `--allow-all-tools` (`runtimeSpawnArgs`). `.pr-review.example.yaml` explicitly advertises `skill_packs:` as a per-repo key.

Attack: a contributor's PR adds `.pr-review.yaml` with `skill_packs: [{git: https://evil.example/prompts}]`. A maintainer who reviews that branch locally (the documented workflow — `detectStack` reads the checkout's manifests precisely because cwd is expected to be the PR's checkout) silently clones the attacker repo and feeds its markdown to a tool-enabled agent as pass rules. `isSafeGitSource` only blocks exotic transports; it does not address *who* declared the source.

Fix: treat pack sources as a user-owned trust decision. Honour `skill_packs` only from the global `~/.pr-review/config.yaml` (and CLI flags), and for a repo-yaml pack that is not already in the global list, refuse to clone it — print the entry and require an explicit `pr-review packs add` / `--trust-repo-packs` opt-in. At minimum, do not auto-clone a pack that first appeared in a repo yaml.

findings.title: Shipped default skill packs are unpinned — every sync pulls mutable upstream HEAD of third-party prompt repos with no integrity check
findings.body:
OWASP A03 (Software Supply Chain Failures); rule D5 "Unpinned Versions in Production" and the A03 mitigation "lockfile integrity / provenance".

All three `DEFAULT_PACKS` entries omit `ref:`, so `ensurePacks`/`syncPacks` clone the default branch and `git pull --ff-only` whatever upstream HEAD is at the time. These packs are prompt content executed as review-pass rules by agents with tool access, and one of them (`mukul975/Anthropic-Cybersecurity-Skills`) is an individual account — a force-push, account takeover, or a malicious commit lands in every user's next review with no version boundary and no way to know what changed. `writeMeta` records the resulting commit but nothing ever verifies it against an expected value.

This contradicts the repo's own `add-pack` skill, which tells users `ref: <branch-or-tag>  # pin for reproducibility (recommended)`.

Fix: pin `ref:` to a tag or commit for each entry in `DEFAULT_PACKS` and bump it deliberately as part of a release; on sync, compare the resolved `HEAD` against the pinned ref and fail the pack (warn + skip) on a mismatch rather than silently adopting new prompt content.

findings.title: Git origin URL is logged verbatim and can leak embedded CI credentials
findings.body:
OWASP A09 / rule S5 "Secrets in CI/CD Pipeline Logs".

`defaultGitRemote` runs `git remote get-url origin` and this note interpolates the raw URL. In CI the origin very often carries credentials in the userinfo component — GitLab CI uses `https://gitlab-ci-token:<job-token>@gitlab.com/...`, Azure Pipelines and Jenkins similarly embed a PAT — so the token ends up in the note.

That note is written to stderr in `runReview` (`for (const n of stack.notes) process.stderr.write(...)`, i.e. into CI build logs and `detached.log`), and on `--context-only` it is also persisted into `pr-review-summary.md` in the run dir.

Fix: redact userinfo before logging, e.g. `const shown = origin?.replace(/\/\/[^@\/]+@/, '//***@') ?? 'none'` (or parse with `new URL()` and clear `username`/`password`), and use `shown` in the note. Apply the same redaction anywhere else an origin/remote URL is echoed.

findings.title: Untrusted skills.sh API response is printed to the terminal without control-character stripping
findings.body:
OWASP A09 / rule L4 "Log Injection" — third-party data reaches the terminal unescaped.

`searchSkillsSh` fetches an undocumented public endpoint and `packsSuggest` prints `h.name` and `h.source` straight through `console.log`. A hostile or compromised response can embed ANSI escape sequences / carriage returns to rewrite the rendered output — including the very next line, `install the repo: pr-review packs add <repo>`, which the user is being invited to copy and run. This PR already added `printable()` in `src/plugins/builtin.ts` for exactly this hazard on pack strings, but it is not applied here.

The same gap exists for git's own stderr in `src/packs/sync.ts:206` and `:260`: `firstLine(err)` forwards remote-controlled `remote: ...` text into warnings printed unfiltered.

Fix: wrap third-party strings in `printable()` (or an equivalent control-character strip) before printing — `console.log(\`  ${printable(h.name)} ... ${printable(h.source)}\`)` — and do the same for the `firstLine(err)` warning bodies.

findings.title: Comment names the wrong cap constant (`MAX_PASSES` vs `MAX_TOTAL_PASSES`)
findings.body:
Rule violated: **outdated/inaccurate comment** — a comment must remain accurate as the code evolves, and this one already doesn't match it.

The budget comment says the union file "concatenates up to `MAX_PASSES` bodies", but `MAX_PASSES` is not the cap that governs this file. It lives in `src/dispatch/pass-select.ts` and is the *fallback* cap (10) used only when project skills become the passes. The ceiling actually enforced on the union file is `MAX_TOTAL_PASSES = 16`, declared eight lines below in this same block (`prepareSessionContext` does `afterTriage.slice(0, MAX_TOTAL_PASSES)`).

Anyone re-sizing `UNION_FILE_CAP` from this comment would compute the budget from 10 bodies instead of 16.

Fix: change the line to reference the local constant, e.g. `// to MAX_TOTAL_PASSES bodies, so it gets a larger budget. Truncation always warns.`

findings.title: `SessionContext` doc comments omit the `context` route and the `project` skills file
findings.body:
Rule violated: **comment doesn't match the code** — both JSDoc lines enumerate the possible values but the enumerations are incomplete, and the missing entry is this PR's headline feature (project skills as shared context).

- Line 177: `/** One row per known skill: dispatched / index / skipped. */` — `PassRoute.matchedBy` is `MatchedBy | 'context' | 'index' | 'skipped'`, and `prepareSessionContext` pushes a `matchedBy: 'context'` row for every project skill. A reader (or a `--resume` shape validator author) taking this list as exhaustive would miss the whole project-rules category that `summarizePasses` renders.
- Line 178: `/** pass name → its pass-*.md; plus 'all' → the union file ... */` — the record also carries a `'project'` key (`skillsFiles['project'] = projectPath`), which `buildOrchestratorPrompt` and `runReview`'s codex wiring both read.

Fix: `/** One row per known skill: dispatched / project context / index / skipped. Persisted as passes.json. */` and `/** pass name → its pass-*.md; plus 'all' → the union file and 'project' → skills-project.md. */`

findings.title: `matchedOn` doc doesn't describe the mixed tag+glob case it can hold
findings.body:
Rule violated: **comment doesn't match the code**.

The doc promises "the matching globs (glob) or stack tags (tag)" — i.e. `matchedOn` holds globs when `matchedBy === 'glob'`. But `selectPasses` has a branch that pushes `candidate(s, 'glob', [...tagHits, ...globHits])` for the extension-only-glob-plus-stack-identity case, so a `glob` row's `matchedOn` can legitimately be a mix of stack tags and globs. The `--context-only` `Matched on` column renders exactly that mix, and `tests/pass-select.test.ts:53` asserts it ("matchedOn carries both signals").

Fix: `/** What hit: matching globs and/or stack tags (an extension-only glob hit also lists the tags that qualified it); [] for repo/forced/baseline. */`

findings.title: `isLanguageGlob` rationale cites "all 10 slots" but the stack cap is now 6
findings.body:
Rule violated: **outdated comment** — the number in the rationale no longer matches the constant a reader sees 60 lines above.

The JSDoc says "a TypeScript PR filled all 10 slots with framework guides", but stack-matched pack passes are capped by `MAX_STACK_PASSES = 6` (line 14); 10 is `MAX_PASSES`, the unrelated project-skill fallback cap. The observation was true under the old cap, but as written it reads as a claim about today's code.

Fix: drop the number, e.g. "...a TypeScript PR filled every stack-pass slot with framework guides for frameworks the repo doesn't use."

findings.title: `parseGlobList` JSDoc says "glob-list" but the function also normalizes `tags`
findings.body:
Rule violated: **would a better name eliminate the comment? refactor instead** / comment narrower than the code.

The JSDoc describes the value as a glob list and the inline comment justifies the brace-aware split with `**/*.{ts,tsx}` — but `loadSkillFile` calls it for a non-glob field too: `tags: parseGlobList(meta.tags)`. Tags never contain braces, so the documented rationale doesn't apply there and the name/doc misdescribe half the call sites.

Fix: either rename to something value-neutral (`parseStringList`) and reword the JSDoc as "Normalize a list-or-CSV frontmatter value (globs, tags); braces are kept intact so `**/*.{ts,tsx}` stays one entry", or add a dedicated tag parser and keep this one glob-only.

findings.title: Dead-code caveat on `loadBuiltInReviewers` should be a tracked annotation
findings.body:
Rule violated: **annotation conventions** — a comment saying code is only kept until something else changes is a TODO/DEPRECATED note and should be marked as one so it is greppable and doesn't rot silently.

`loadBuiltInReviewers()` now unconditionally returns `[]`; the second line, "Kept only until the loader drops it", records an intended deletion with no marker, so no `TODO`/`DEPRECATED` scan will ever surface it.

Fix: `// TODO: remove once the loader stops calling this — there are no built-in reviewers; every review pass is a skill selected at review time (packs + repo skills).`

findings.title: "Formerly agents/verifier.md" is history maintained in a comment
findings.body:
Rule violated: **changelog comments** — don't keep migration history in comments; git history and CHANGELOG.md already carry it, and the line becomes stale noise as soon as nobody remembers the old file.

The first two lines of the `VERIFIER_BRIEF` JSDoc explain *why* the verifier survives as a pipeline step — that part is a good WHY comment. The trailing "Formerly agents/verifier.md." adds only provenance for a file this PR deletes.

Fix: drop that sentence (the deletion of `agents/verifier.md` is already in this PR's diff and in CHANGELOG.md).

findings.title: Decorative divider comments in the new test sections
findings.body:
Rule violated: **divider comments** — decorative `// --- X ---` banners are listed as an anti-pattern; the code structure (the `describe`/`test` names and the helper below) already says what the section is.

`tests/config.test.ts:148` adds `// --- skill_packs ---`, which restates the very next helper and the test names underneath it. The sibling at `tests/frontmatter.test.ts:71` (`// --- pack-format support: applyTo CSV, tags, frontmatter name, heading fallback ---`) has the same shape, though it at least carries a content summary.

Fix: delete the pure divider at `tests/config.test.ts:148`; if grouping needs to be visible, wrap the block in a `describe('skill_packs', ...)` so the label shows up in test output instead of only in the source.

findings.title: One unreadable pack file aborts the entire review instead of degrading
Swallowed metadata-write failure makes `packs sync` report success while every review says "stale"
findings.body:
The `catch { // best-effort }` around `writeFileSync(packMetaPath(...))` discards the error entirely — it is neither surfaced to the caller nor logged. The failure is not cosmetic: `packMetaPath` is the only freshness record, so when the write fails (EACCES on `~/.pr-review/packs`, ENOSPC, a read-only home in CI) `syncPacks` still pushes the pack into `result.synced` and `packs sync` prints `✓ <name>`, while `packStatus` reads back `meta: null` → `ageDays: null` → every subsequent review prints "last sync unknown age — run `pr-review packs sync`" and `doctor` marks the pack bad. The user is told to run a command that keeps reporting success, and the actual cause is never written anywhere.

Rule (OWASP Error Handling — error details must be logged for investigation, and a failed operation must not be reported as a success): log it and let the caller know the sync only half-completed, e.g. have `writeMeta` return `{ meta, metaWritten: false }` (or throw) so `syncPacks` records it under `failed`, and at minimum emit `process.stderr.write(\`[packs] ${pack.name}: could not write ${packMetaPath(pack, home)} — freshness tracking disabled (${(err as Error).message.split('\n')[0]})\n\`)` instead of the empty catch. The same applies to the `rev-parse`/`log` catch above it, which silently produces `commit: undefined` and the `?` shown by `packs list`.

findings.title: readdir failure silently yields zero skills, so the run blames pack config instead of the I/O error
findings.body:
`catch { return []; }` turns any enumeration failure (EACCES on the pack dir, EMFILE, a dir replaced mid-sync) into "this pack has no skills", with nothing logged. Downstream that becomes a misleading diagnosis: pass selection finds nothing, and `runReview` exits 2 with "nothing to review with — no skills matched this PR (stack tags: …); run `pr-review packs suggest …` or configure skill_packs", while `packs list`/`doctor` show the pack as `✓ 0 skill(s)`. Every message points the user at pack configuration or stack detection; none names the real failure.

Rule (OWASP Error Handling — log the error server-side for investigation rather than swallowing it, and don't return a generic outcome that misattributes the cause): keep the empty return, but write one warning first — `process.stderr.write(\`[packs] warning: cannot list ${printable(dir)} — pack contributes no skills (${printable((err as Error).message.split('\n')[0] ?? '')})\n\`)` — so a zero-pass run can be told apart from an unreadable checkout.

findings.title: git error text is echoed verbatim and can carry credentials embedded in a pack URL
findings.body:
`firstLine(err)` returns git's raw stderr and it is echoed unmodified into user-visible output: `warnings.push(\`[packs] ${pack.name}: clone failed — ${firstLine(err)}; continuing without it\`)` (line 206, printed on every review) and `result.failed.push({ ..., error: firstLine(err) + hint })` (line 260, printed by `packs sync`). `isSafeGitSource` deliberately accepts any `https://` URL — including the private-mirror form `https://user:token@host/org/repo.git` the docs mention — and git reports failures as `fatal: unable to access 'https://user:token@host/org/repo.git/': …` / `Authentication failed for 'https://user:token@…'`. The token therefore lands in stderr, in the detached run log under `~/.pr-review/runs/`, and in CI job logs, which are usually visible to more people than the secret is.

Rule (OWASP Error Handling — error messages must not carry details beyond what the recipient needs; the detail belongs in a controlled log, not in text that gets copied around): redact userinfo before echoing, in `firstLine` so both call sites are covered:

```ts
return (text.split('\n')[0] ?? 'unknown error').replace(/\/\/[^/@\s]+@/g, '//***@');
```

The same redaction should be applied wherever `pack.git` itself is printed (`packs list`, `doctor`'s not-cloned message).

findings.title: git origin URL (may embed credentials) is logged verbatim to stderr, detached.log, and the run summary
Configured pack git URL is echoed unmasked by `doctor`, `packs list`, and the duplicate-name warning
findings.body:
**Rule (OWASP Logging Cheat Sheet — "Data to exclude"):** never record access tokens or connection strings directly; mask or remove them first.

`pack.git` is whatever the user put in `skill_packs:` — and the config explicitly documents "a full git URL" as a supported form, which is how a private pack gets authenticated (`https://x-access-token:<token>@github.com/org/private-pack.git`). That value is printed verbatim in four new places:

- here, in `pr-review doctor` — the one command whose output users routinely paste into bug reports and chat
- `src/commands/packs.ts:34` — `packs list` not-cloned line
- `src/config.ts:210` — the duplicate-pack-name warning `(${p.git})`
- `src/packs/sync.ts:104` — `writeMeta` persists `git: pack.git` into `~/.pr-review/packs/<name>.json` in cleartext

**Fix:** run the URL through a redactor before printing (and before storing it in the meta JSON), e.g. a shared `redactUrl(u) => u.replace(/\/\/[^@/]+@/, '//***@')` in `src/packs/sync.ts` used by all four call sites:

```ts
bad(`pack ${pack.name}`, `not cloned (${redactUrl(pack.git)}) — clones on the next review, or run \`pr-review packs sync\``);
```

findings.title: git error text is logged without control-character sanitization (CR log forging) despite `printable()` existing for exactly this
A baseline pass is silently dropped when it also stack-matches and overflows the stack cap
findings.body:
`selectPasses` promises that every configured baseline always dispatches (the comment on this line, AGENTS.md "+ EVERY baseline", and the CHANGELOG "every baseline pointer ALWAYS dispatches"). The code does not deliver that.

In the pack loop the baseline check is the *last* tier: a skill that hits a glob or a stack tag is pushed as a `glob`/`tag` candidate and `continue`s, so a baseline skill that also stack-matches never gets a candidate with `matchedBy === 'baseline'`. It then competes for the `MAX_STACK_PASSES` (6) slots, and if it ranks below the cut it lands in `stackOverflow` → `indexEntries`. The `baselines` filter on this line only re-adds candidates whose `matchedBy` is literally `'baseline'`, so it cannot rescue it — and `missingBaseline` stays empty, so nothing warns.

Verified by running the module directly (7 pack skills all matching `**/main.go`, one of them the configured baseline, stack tag `go`):

```
passes: [ pk/a:glob, pk/b:glob, pk/c:glob, pk/d:glob, pk/e:glob, pk/f:glob ]
baseline dispatched? false
in index?          true
missingBaseline:   []
```

This is exactly the coverage-starvation failure this release claims to have fixed: a security/error-handling baseline can be evicted from a code PR with no warning. It triggers whenever a baseline's name/tags overlap a stack tag (e.g. a dependency literally named `logging`, or `security`) or a pack's baseline carries `applyTo` globs — and `.claude/skills/add-pack.md` actively instructs users to configure their own `baseline:` pointers, so user-configured packs hit it easily.

Fix: keep baselines out of the capped competition entirely, so they keep their higher-tier label but can never overflow:

```ts
const stackCandidates = candidates
  .filter((c) => (c.pass.matchedBy === 'glob' || c.pass.matchedBy === 'tag') && !baselineSet.has(c.skill.name))
  .sort(/* unchanged */);
// ...
const baselines = candidates.filter((c) => baselineSet.has(c.skill.name) && !keptNames.has(c.pass.name));
```

The existing `baseline dedupe keeps the higher tier` test still passes (the row keeps `matchedBy: 'glob'`); add a case with `MAX_STACK_PASSES + 1` stack candidates where one is the baseline.

findings.title: skills-all.md is written every run but read by nobody whenever project skills exist
findings.body:
`authoritativeSkills = ctx.skillsFiles['project'] ?? unionSkills` makes the union file a *fallback*, not the context it is documented to be. `skills-all.md` is the only consumer target for `unionSkills`, and `skillsFiles['all']` is referenced nowhere else (also `src/commands/review.ts:770` picks `skillsFiles['project'] ?? skillsFiles['all']` for the Codex sibling). So in any repo that has at least one matched project skill — the common case, including this repo — the union file is generated (up to `UNION_FILE_CAP` = 96 KB) and never read by any prompt.

That contradicts documentation shipped in this same PR:
- AGENTS.md: "`skills-all.md` (union read by codex/companions/verifier)"
- `.claude/skills/debug-review-run.md`: "Union of all pass bodies — read by the Codex sibling, companion agents, and the verifier"
- CHANGELOG 0.7.0 says both "they now read `skills-all.md`" *and* "Codex, companions, and the verifier read the project rules" — the two statements disagree with each other.

Beyond the docs drift, it is a real coverage change: the second-opinion Codex reviewer and the verifier lose every pack lens (OWASP, security-and-owasp, the stack passes) the moment a repo defines one project skill.

Fix: pick one and make code and docs agree. Either pass both files (`skillsRulesSentence` already takes one path — extend it, or concatenate project rules into the union file so `skills-all.md` carries project-first + pass bodies), or drop `renderUnionFile`/`skills-all.md` entirely and correct AGENTS.md, the debug-review-run skill, and the CHANGELOG line that still claims codex/companions read the union.

findings.title: PassSelection.routes is dead in production — the shipped routing table is recomputed elsewhere
findings.body:
`selectPasses` builds and returns `routes`, but nothing in `src/` ever reads `selection.routes` (grep for `.routes` over `src/` returns no matches). The routing table that actually ships — written to `passes.json` and rendered into the `## Skills` summary — is rebuilt independently in `prepareSessionContext` as `routing`, and the two are not equivalent: `prepareSessionContext`'s version additionally emits `skipped` rows (`--skip`, docs-only triage) and cap-overflow rows that `selectPasses.routes` never produces.

The only consumers of `routes` are `tests/pass-select.test.ts` (lines 135, 181, 224), so the assertions about routing are made against a value users never see, while the artifact they do see (`passes.json`, the resume path's shape validation) is covered only indirectly. Two implementations of the same table will drift.

Fix: delete `routes` from `PassSelection` and retarget those three assertions at `prepareSessionContext(...).routing`, or make `prepareSessionContext` consume `selection.routes` (appending its skip/overflow rows) instead of rebuilding it.

findings.title: Stack pass ranking counts globs, not diff coverage — this PR's own run spent 5 of 6 slots on markdown/Azure guides
findings.body:
`matchedOn.length` ranks candidates by *how many globs/tags a skill declared*, not by how much of the diff it actually covers. A pack author who writes `applyTo: '**/*.ts, **/*.js, **/*.json'` outranks one who writes `**/*.ts`, and one topic family can take every slot.

This run proves it (`passes.json`): on a ~2000-line TypeScript diff the six stack passes were `azure-functions-typescript` (ranked first purely because it lists 3 extensions; this repo has no Azure Functions), `nodejs-javascript-vitest`, and then `markdown`, `markdown-accessibility`, `markdown-content-creation`, `markdown-gfm` — four near-duplicate doc-format lenses. No general TypeScript/Node code lens ran at all, which is the exact failure the `isLanguageGlob` guard was added to prevent.

Fix: rank by *files matched* (count the in-scope paths a skill's globs hit, which `globHits` already discards) instead of `matchedOn.length`, and cap how many kept passes may share a leading name token so one family cannot crowd out the rest of the stack.

findings.title: skills-all.md is written but referenced by nothing whenever project skills exist
findings.body:
`authoritativeSkills = ctx.skillsFiles['project'] ?? unionSkills` means that as soon as the repo has one matched project skill, the union file drops out of every companion, verifier, and codex prompt (`review.ts:770` does the same for the Codex sibling).

Measured on this run: `skills-all.md` is 71 KB and `orchestrator-prompt.md` mentions it 0 times, while `skills-project.md` appears 20 times. So the verifier and codex reconcile with zero pack knowledge, and the file is pure write-amplification. It also contradicts docs shipped in this same PR — AGENTS.md and `.claude/skills/debug-review-run.md` both state `skills-all.md` is "read by the Codex sibling, companion agents, and the verifier".

Pick one and make code and docs agree: either give those prompts both paths (project rules first, union as reference), or stop writing the union file (and delete `renderUnionFile`) when project skills are present.

findings.title: syncPacks duplicates ensurePacks' clone block and drops its partial-clone cleanup
findings.body:
The clone sequence (safety guard → `mkdirSync` → build `clone --depth 1 --single-branch [--branch ref]` → `rev-parse --verify HEAD`) exists verbatim in both `ensurePacks` (lines 181-192) and here, but only `ensurePacks` has the `rmSync` cleanup in its catch.

Failure: `packs sync` is interrupted or the `rev-parse --verify HEAD` guard throws on a commit-less clone. `syncPacks` reports the failure and leaves the directory behind; every later `packs sync` then takes the `!isGitCheckout(dir)` branch and fails with "exists but is not a git checkout", and every review warns the same, until the user deletes it by hand. The comment at line 191 shows this case was anticipated — the cleanup just did not get copied along with the code.

Extract one `clonePack(pack, dir, git)` helper carrying the guard, the argv, the verify, and the cleanup-on-throw, and call it from both paths.

findings.title: A baseline skill inside an index-mode pack is silently dropped and never reported as missing
findings.body:
`mode === 'index'` short-circuits to `indexSkills` before the `baselineSet.has(s.name)` check, so a baseline configured on an index pack never dispatches. `missingBaseline` (line 251) only tests membership in `packNames`, which index skills are in — so nothing warns either.

Concrete case: a user copies the shipped `anthropic-cybersecurity` entry (`mode: index`) and adds `baseline: ['secure-coding']`. The pass never runs and no output mentions it, which breaks the invariant this PR documents — "a pointer that no longer resolves surfaces as a `missingBaseline` warning" — for a pointer that resolves but can never fire.

Cheapest fix: in `missingBaseline`, also report baselines whose skill was found in an `index` pack ("baseline X is in an index-only pack and will never run"), or reject `baseline` + `mode: index` in `normalizePack` at config load.

findings.title: skillsFiles mixes pass names with the reserved keys 'all' and 'project'
findings.body:
`skillsFiles[p.name]` shares one map with `skillsFiles['all']` and `skillsFiles['project']`, which are written after the pass loop. Repo skills keep their plain name (only pack skills are `<pack>/<skill>`), so a repo skill at `.claude/skills/all/SKILL.md` — or `project/SKILL.md` in the no-packs fallback where project skills become passes — silently loses its own file: line 562's `ctx.skillsFiles[p.name]!` then hands that pass the union/project file, and it applies the wrong rules under its own reviewer name.

Simpler and collision-proof: keep only pass files in the map and put the two singletons on `SessionContext` as typed fields (`unionPath?`, `projectPath?`). That also removes the stringly-typed lookups at `review.ts:770` and line 540.

findings.title: runDoctor dynamic-imports node:fs and re-evaluates its probes twice
findings.body:
Every other dependency in this file is a static top-level import; these four `await import(...)` calls buy nothing (the packs block runs unconditionally on every `doctor` invocation) and make the function harder to read. `gitAvailable()` is then called twice on line 72 and `existsSync(linguistCachePath())` twice more at lines 90-92.

Move the four imports to the top of the file and hoist the two probes into `const git = gitAvailable()` / `const linguistCached = existsSync(linguistCachePath())`.

findings.title: loadConfig home ternary repeated four times in packs.ts
findings.body: `loadConfig(opts.home ? { homeOverride: opts.home } : {})` appears in `packsList`, `packsSync`, `packsAdd`, and `packsSuggest`. `loadConfig` already does `opts.homeOverride ?? homedir()` (config.ts:274), so `loadConfig({ homeOverride: opts.home })` is identical for `undefined` — drop the ternary in all four places.

findings.title: Duplicate node:fs import
findings.body: Lines 1-2 import from `'node:fs'` twice. Merge into `import { readdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';`.

findings.title: skills-all.md is documented as read by codex/companions/verifier, but nothing reads it when project skills exist
findings.body:
`renderUnionFile`'s doc says the union file is "read by codex, companions, and the verifier", and the same claim is repeated at `src/dispatch/single-session.ts:178` (`skillsFiles` doc) and in six docs this PR touches: `AGENTS.md:22`, `.claude/skills/debug-review-run.md:16`, `README.md:163`, `skills/help/reference/architecture.md:36`, `companion-plugins.md:40`, `reviewers-vs-skills.md:49-50`.

The wiring says otherwise. `single-session.ts:540` computes `authoritativeSkills = ctx.skillsFiles['project'] ?? unionSkills` and feeds that to companions (line 549) and the verifier (line 616); `src/commands/review.ts:770` passes the same `skillsFiles['project'] ?? skillsFiles['all']` to codex; and the pass prompts (line 562) pass only `skillsFiles['project']`. Meanwhile the union file is written unconditionally whenever `passes.length > 0`.

So on any repo with matched project skills — the normal case, and the case in this very run, where every dispatched prompt points at `skills-project.md` — `skills-all.md` is generated and read by nobody. A maintainer debugging "why did codex not see the OWASP skill" will open the wrong artifact, which is exactly what `debug-review-run.md` sends them to do.

Fix: reword to what line 540 actually implements — "the FALLBACK context for codex/companions/verifier; `skills-project.md` wins when any project skill matched" — and correct the same sentence at line 178 plus the six doc echoes. Alternatively, if the union really is meant to reach those readers, append it alongside the project file instead of being displaced by it.

findings.title: `includeCodex` doc describes a behaviour this module does not have (and the field is never read)
findings.body:
`/** When the Codex sibling reviewer will run, it reads the union skills file too. */` documents a conditional that does not exist here: `opts.includeCodex` is declared on line 61 and referenced nowhere else in `src/` (only `review.ts:673` passes it in). The union file's creation is gated on `passes.length > 0` (lines 461-466), not on codex; and codex's skills path is chosen in `review.ts:770`, outside this module.

The result is a dead option whose only documentation asserts a cause-and-effect relationship that no code implements — the worst kind of comment, because it reads as a design constraint and will be defended in a future refactor.

Fix: delete the field and its comment (and the `includeCodex` argument at `review.ts:673`); or, if gating the union file on codex is the intent, implement it and keep the comment.

findings.title: Union-budget comment cites `MAX_PASSES`, a constant from another module that means something else
findings.body:
The comment reads "The union file (codex/companions/verifier) concatenates up to MAX_PASSES bodies, so it gets a larger budget." The ceiling that actually bounds `renderUnionFile` is `MAX_TOTAL_PASSES = 16`, declared eight lines below (line 93) and applied at line 432 (`afterTriage.slice(0, MAX_TOTAL_PASSES)`).

`MAX_PASSES` is a *different* constant in a *different* module: `src/dispatch/pass-select.ts:16`, value 10, documented there as "Fallback cap when project skills ARE the passes (no packs configured)". It never bounds the union.

Failure scenario: someone tuning `UNION_FILE_CAP` greps `MAX_PASSES`, finds 10, and sizes the budget for 10 bodies while 16 can arrive — silent truncation of the last passes' skill bodies (the code warns, but the sizing decision was already made on a false premise).

Fix: change `MAX_PASSES` to `MAX_TOTAL_PASSES` in this comment.

findings.title: "10-pass cap" is not any cap in the code — and this file is injected into every review pass
findings.body:
This added line tells a debugger that a skill missing from the pass table may have overflowed "the 10-pass cap". There is no 10-pass cap. The caps are `MAX_STACK_PASSES = 6` (`src/dispatch/pass-select.ts:14`, stack passes only) and `MAX_TOTAL_PASSES = 16` (`src/dispatch/single-session.ts:93`, hard ceiling); baselines ride on top of the 6 and are never trimmed to 10.

This is worse than an ordinary stale doc: `.claude/skills/` files are repo skills, so every matched one is rendered into `skills-project.md` and injected into EVERY dispatched pass as authoritative project rules — this file is in the current run's `skills-project.md`. The wrong number is being handed to reviewers as fact.

It also contradicts line 17 of this same file ("overflow past the pass cap") and `.claude/skills/add-pack.md:47`, which both get it right.

Fix: "overflow past the stack-pass cap (`MAX_STACK_PASSES` = 6; baselines ride on top)".

findings.title: "At most 10 passes dispatch per review" contradicts both the code and the sibling reference page
findings.body:
Added line: "At most 10 passes dispatch per review; overflow joins the index." The actual selection is up to 6 stack passes (`MAX_STACK_PASSES`, `src/dispatch/pass-select.ts:14`) PLUS every baseline pointer (7 with the shipped `DEFAULT_PACKS`), hard-capped at `MAX_TOTAL_PASSES = 16` (`src/dispatch/single-session.ts:93`).

`skills/help/reference/reviewers-vs-skills.md:33`, added in this same PR, states it correctly: "at most `MAX_STACK_PASSES = 6` stack passes dispatch; baselines ride on top (typically 7, so <=13 passes)". Two user-facing help pages now give incompatible numbers, and this one is the page a user reads while deciding how many skills to write.

Fix: replace with the 6-stack + baselines wording (or defer to reviewers-vs-skills.md rather than restating a number that must now be kept in sync in two places).

findings.title: "validate before caching" claims a check `parseLinguist` does not perform
findings.body:
The trailing comment on `const index = parseLinguist(text); // validate before caching` implies bad content is rejected before `writeFileSync`. `parseLinguist` only throws on a YAML *syntax* error: any body that parses to a non-object falls through the `if (doc && typeof doc === 'object')` guard at lines 43-56 and returns a structurally valid but EMPTY index, which is then cached.

Failure scenario: a proxy or captive portal answers 200 with an HTML page, or the response is truncated mid-file. The empty/partial index is written to `~/.pr-review/cache/linguist-languages.yml`; from then on the cached-first branch (lines 88-91) returns it forever, because `readCache()` is non-null whenever the file parses. Language tags silently stay empty (or partial) on every subsequent review — including after `packs sync`, which only force-refreshes, and falls back to this same cache when the refresh fails. Stack detection degrades with no warning, which is precisely the failure this comment promises to prevent.

Fix: make the comment true rather than deleting the check — `if (index.byExt.size === 0) throw new Error('unusable languages.yml');` before writing the cache, and treat an empty cached index as a cache miss at line 90.

findings.title: "mirrors loadSkillFile naming" is false for any pack file that declares a frontmatter `name:`
findings.body:
`skillNameOf` derives the name from the pack-relative path alone. `loadSkillFile` does not: `src/plugins/builtin.ts:119,126` computes `normalizeSkillName(declaredName ?? inferNameFromPath(filePath))`, so a frontmatter `name:` wins over the filename. The two "mirror" each other only while every pack file's frontmatter agrees with its directory name.

The divergence is not cosmetic — `skillNameOf` exists solely to power the exclude-by-name half of `listPackFiles` (line 46), and that is the control keeping operational/offensive SecOps skills out of review context (`DEFAULT_PACKS.anthropic-cybersecurity.exclude` in `src/config.ts`). A pack file at `skills/generic-helper/SKILL.md` with `name: hunting-lateral-movement` loads under the excluded name but is matched against `generic-helper`, so the exclude misses and the skill lands in the index. It fails silently and in the permissive direction. (The three shipped packs happen to agree today — I checked — which is why this will not surface until a pack changes upstream.)

Fix: state the limitation ("path-derived name; a frontmatter `name:` is NOT consulted, so exclude-by-name is best-effort"), or read the frontmatter name here so the mirror is real.

findings.title: `matchedOn` doc omits the 'glob' rows that carry no globs, and the triage comment inherits the error
findings.body:
The doc says `matchedOn` is "the matching globs (glob) or stack tags (tag); [] for repo/forced/baseline" — enumerating exactly which labels yield an empty array. But line 186 pushes untargeted project skills as `candidate(s, 'glob', [])`: matchedBy 'glob' with zero globs, because "empty applies_to = always applies".

Two things the comment hides:
- The `## Passes` / `## Skills` tables render `glob | —` for a skill that matched no file at all, which reads as a bug to anyone using the table to debug routing.
- `triagePasses` in `src/dispatch/single-session.ts:184` is commented "Docs-only PRs run only passes pinned to files (glob) or forced" and filters on `matchedBy === 'glob'`. An untargeted project skill is not pinned to files, yet survives docs-only triage. Whether or not that is desired, both comments currently describe a rule the code does not implement.

Fix: either document the third case here ("…or [] when an untargeted project skill always applies") and reword the triage comment, or give always-applies project skills a distinct label so 'glob' keeps its stated meaning.

findings.title: Comment justifies skipping Linguist on a premise that misses its second consumer
findings.body:
"No packs configured → language tags feed nothing glob/tag-matched" is true for pass selection, but the tags have a second consumer the comment does not mention: `selection.stackTags` is written into `pr-context.md`'s `## Stack` block (`src/dispatch/single-session.ts:248`), which every dispatched pass reads as the PR's stack description.

With `skill_packs: []` — the documented fallback where project skills become the passes — that block silently degrades to manifest/ecosystem tags with no languages, and nothing in the run reports why. The comment as written tells the next maintainer the skip is free.

Fix: name the tradeoff ("…and the `## Stack` block in pr-context.md degrades to manifest tags only"), or keep the load when it costs nothing: `config.skillPacks.length > 0 || existsSync(linguistCachePath(opts.homeOverride))`.

findings.title: "The generic subagent type both runtimes accept" is asserted as fact but verified on one runtime
findings.body:
This PR's own description states the Copilot runtime could not be exercised: "Declared not-verifiable here: Copilot runtime (binary not on PATH — `GENERIC_AGENT` is the single line to adjust if its generic agent type differs)". The comment states cross-runtime acceptance flatly, so the one place recording the uncertainty is the PR body — which disappears the moment the PR merges, while the comment stays and reads as settled.

Failure scenario: a Copilot run returns zero findings because `task(agent_type: 'general-purpose')` is rejected; the maintainer reads this comment, concludes the agent type is fine, and looks elsewhere.

Fix: keep the fact, drop the certainty — "'general-purpose' is Claude Code's built-in generic subagent type; assumed compatible with Copilot's `task` tool but not yet verified against it — this is the single line to change if Copilot names it differently."

findings.title: Transitional comment ("until the loader drops it") on a dead stub with no removal trigger
findings.body:
`loadBuiltInReviewers()` now returns `[]`, and its comment ends "Kept only until the loader drops it." That is a snapshot of an in-progress refactor: no issue, no date, no owner, and no way for a future reader to tell whether the moment has passed. Comments describing a transitional state rot fastest, and this one will outlive everyone's memory of the 0.7.0 migration.

The event it waits for is one line away in this same PR: `src/plugins/loader.ts:184` is the sole caller, inside `if (includeBuiltIn && !skillsOnly)`, and the review path always passes `skillsOnly: true`.

Fix: delete the function and the `includeBuiltIn` branch now (the diff is three lines), or keep the function and replace the comment with the durable fact alone — "There are no built-in reviewers: every review pass is a skill selected at review time" — with no forward-looking clause.

findings.title: No test covers a baseline that also stack-matches but loses the MAX_STACK_PASSES cap — the "baselines always dispatch" invariant silently breaks
findings.body:
`selectPasses` promises that every baseline runs (`tests/pass-select.test.ts` even asserts *"baselines can no longer be starved out"*), but the guarantee only holds for baselines that match **nothing else**.

A baseline skill that ALSO hits a glob/tag gets pushed as a `glob`/`tag` candidate and `continue`s before the `baselineSet.has(s.name)` branch ever runs. It is therefore absent from `candidates.filter((c) => c.pass.matchedBy === 'baseline')` here. If it then lands outside `stackCandidates.slice(0, MAX_STACK_PASSES)`, it goes to `stackOverflow` → the on-demand index and is **never dispatched at all**.

Failure scenario: a pack configures `baseline: ['nodejs-security']` (the documented per-pack baseline pattern) and that skill has `tags: [node]`. On a Node PR with 6+ other stack-matching skills, `nodejs-security` sorts below the cap → dropped to the index, no warning, `missingBaseline` empty. Every review of that repo silently loses its declared baseline lens.

The existing dedupe test (`baseline dedupe keeps the higher tier`) only exercises the case where the dual-matched baseline is *inside* the cap, so it gives false confidence.

Suggested test: build `MAX_STACK_PASSES + 2` glob candidates where one of them is named in `baseline`, and assert it is still present in `sel.passes` (not in `indexEntries`).

findings.title: The symlink-containment guard on pack files has zero test coverage
findings.body:
`containedIn` is the only thing stopping a third-party pack (arbitrary git repos cloned from user config, read by agents with tool access) from pulling arbitrary local files into agent context via a symlink — the comment on it says exactly that. Yet no test in `tests/packs-load.test.ts` ever creates a symlink inside a pack dir: the tests only cover include/exclude globs, index mode, and duplicate names.

Failure scenario: delete the `.filter((rel) => containedIn(...))` line (or invert the `catch { return false }` to `true`, or break the `base + '/'` prefix check on POSIX after a Windows-only edit) and the entire suite stays green. A pack containing `skills/leak/SKILL.md -> ~/.ssh/id_rsa` or `-> ~/.aws/credentials` would then be loaded as a skill body and shipped into `pass-*.md` / `skills-index.md`, i.e. into every dispatched agent's context.

Suggested test: in a temp pack dir, `symlinkSync` an outside `.md` file into an included path and assert `listPackFiles` excludes it while a real file at the same path is included. Wrap symlink creation in try/catch and `skip` when it throws — CI runs `windows-latest`, where unprivileged symlink creation can fail.

findings.title: A baseline pointing at an index-mode pack skill is neither dispatched nor reported as missing — untested
findings.body:
`missingBaseline` is computed from `packNames`, which includes skills from `mode: 'index'` packs. But index skills `continue` out of the loop before the `baselineSet.has(s.name)` branch, so they can never become a baseline candidate.

Net effect: for a pack configured with `mode: index` and a non-empty `baseline: [...]` (both are documented, independently settable yaml keys), the baseline skill never runs as a pass AND produces no `missingBaseline` warning — the exact silent rot the repo rules say baseline pointers must never have ("break loudly, not silently").

No test covers this combination: `index-only packs never become passes; missing baseline reported` uses a baseline name that is absent from the pack entirely, which takes the other branch.

Suggested test: one pack with `mode: 'index'` whose skill name IS in `baseline`, asserting either that it dispatches or that it lands in `missingBaseline` — pick the intended contract and pin it (reporting it as missing, or rejecting the config at load time, is the cheaper fix).

findings.title: Changed pack `git:` source is untested and unguarded — the old checkout is silently reused and pulled
findings.body:
`syncPacks` carefully guards a changed `ref:` (with a test: `a changed ref: is reported, never silently pulled from the old branch`), but the identical hazard for a changed `git:` has neither guard nor test. `PackMeta` already persists `git`, and nothing ever compares it.

Failure scenario: a user edits `skill_packs` from `- git: acme/rules-v1\n  name: rules` to `git: acme/rules-v2` keeping `name: rules`. `ensurePacks` sees the dir exists and marks it present; `syncPacks` runs `git pull --ff-only` inside the v1 checkout. Every subsequent review is performed with v1's review knowledge while `packs list` prints the pack as fresh and synced — a wrong-content review that reports as healthy. The same applies to a repo yaml that repoints a pack name inherited from the global config.

Suggested test: mirror the ref-change test — `ensurePacks` a pack from remote A, then `syncPacks` the same `name` with `git` pointing at remote B, and assert it is reported in `failed` ("source changed — delete <dir> and re-sync") rather than silently pulled.

findings.title: The post-clone HEAD verification and its cleanup path are untested
findings.body:
`git(['rev-parse', '--verify', 'HEAD'], dir)` exists specifically to catch a clone that produced a `.git` dir with no commit, so the catch block can `rmSync` the partial checkout. Nothing tests it: `a bad source warns and leaves no directory behind` fails at `git clone` itself, so it never reaches this line.

Why the untested branch matters: if this verification is removed or the cleanup is skipped, the empty checkout persists, and every later run takes the `existsSync(dir) && isGitCheckout(dir)` fast path — the pack is reported present and fresh while contributing zero skills forever, with no warning. That is a silent, permanent loss of review knowledge that only a manual `rm -rf` fixes.

Suggested test: `git init -b main` a remote with NO commit (clone succeeds, HEAD unborn), run `ensurePacks`, and assert `present` is empty, a `clone failed` warning is emitted, and `packDir` no longer exists.

findings.title: The MAX_PASSES fallback cap (project skills as passes) is never exercised
findings.body:
In the no-pack-passes fallback, `project.slice(0, MAX_PASSES)` becomes the passes and `project.slice(MAX_PASSES)` is pushed to the index. `MAX_PASSES` is exported but never imported by any test: `fallback with no pack passes: project skills become the passes themselves` uses exactly 2 project skills, so both the cap and the overflow-to-index branch are dead in the suite.

Failure scenario: a repo with `skill_packs: []` and 25 project skills (the configuration the docs recommend for teams that only want their own rules). Swap `MAX_PASSES` for `MAX_STACK_PASSES` here, or invert the slice bounds, and 15+ business-rule skills are silently demoted to the index — or 25 passes are dispatched, blowing the session token budget — with a green suite either way. This is the product's stated core value path (project rules driving the review), so it deserves a pin.

Suggested test: `MAX_PASSES + 2` targeted repo skills, `packSkills: []` — assert `passes.length === MAX_PASSES` and that the 2 overflowed skills appear in `indexEntries` with `matchedBy: 'index'` routes.

findings.title: Test fixture omits the required `projectSkills`, and nothing covers the review.ts → session wiring that injects project rules
findings.body:
`emptySelection()` is annotated `PassSelection` but omits the required `projectSkills` field. It compiles only because `tsconfig.json` excludes `tests/` and `tsx` strips types without checking — so the type annotation buys nothing here, and the whole-pipeline tests run with an input shape the real `selectPasses` can never return.

The consequence is a real hole, not just tidiness: `SingleSessionOptions.projectSkills` is optional (`projectSkills?`) and `prepareSessionContext` defaults it with `?? []`. So if `src/commands/review.ts` stopped forwarding `projectSkills: selection.projectSkills`, `skills-project.md` would never be written and every pass, companion and the verifier would lose the user's authoritative business rules — and all 327 tests would still pass. `session-context.test.ts` covers the downstream half by passing `projectSkills` in by hand; `pass-select.test.ts` covers the upstream half; nothing covers the seam between them.

Suggested: (1) add `projectSkills: []` to the fixture so it matches the real contract; (2) extend one `runReview` test so the injected selection returns a non-empty `projectSkills` and assert `skills-project.md` exists in the run dir and its content reaches the orchestrator prompt. Consider also adding a `tsc --noEmit` pass over `tests/` in CI so fixture drift from production types is caught.
