Beyond the docs drift, it is a real coverage change: the second-opinion Codex reviewer and the verifier lose every pack lens (OWASP, security-and-owasp, the stack passes) the moment a repo defines one project skill.

Fix: pick one and make code and docs agree. Either pass both files (`skillsRulesSentence` already takes one path — extend it, or concatenate project rules into the union file so `skills-all.md` carries project-first + pass bodies), or drop `renderUnionFile`/`skills-all.md` entirely and correct AGENTS.md, the debug-review-run skill, and the CHANGELOG line that still claims codex/companions read the union.

finalFindings.title: PassSelection.routes is dead in production — the shipped routing table is recomputed elsewhere
finalFindings.body:
`selectPasses` builds and returns `routes`, but nothing in `src/` ever reads `selection.routes` (grep for `.routes` over `src/` returns no matches). The routing table that actually ships — written to `passes.json` and rendered into the `## Skills` summary — is rebuilt independently in `prepareSessionContext` as `routing`, and the two are not equivalent: `prepareSessionContext`'s version additionally emits `skipped` rows (`--skip`, docs-only triage) and cap-overflow rows that `selectPasses.routes` never produces.

The only consumers of `routes` are `tests/pass-select.test.ts` (lines 135, 181, 224), so the assertions about routing are made against a value users never see, while the artifact they do see (`passes.json`, the resume path's shape validation) is covered only indirectly. Two implementations of the same table will drift.

Fix: delete `routes` from `PassSelection` and retarget those three assertions at `prepareSessionContext(...).routing`, or make `prepareSessionContext` consume `selection.routes` (appending its skip/overflow rows) instead of rebuilding it.

finalFindings.title: Stack pass ranking counts globs, not diff coverage — this PR's own run spent 5 of 6 slots on markdown/Azure guides
finalFindings.body:
`matchedOn.length` ranks candidates by *how many globs/tags a skill declared*, not by how much of the diff it actually covers. A pack author who writes `applyTo: '**/*.ts, **/*.js, **/*.json'` outranks one who writes `**/*.ts`, and one topic family can take every slot.

This run proves it (`passes.json`): on a ~2000-line TypeScript diff the six stack passes were `azure-functions-typescript` (ranked first purely because it lists 3 extensions; this repo has no Azure Functions), `nodejs-javascript-vitest`, and then `markdown`, `markdown-accessibility`, `markdown-content-creation`, `markdown-gfm` — four near-duplicate doc-format lenses. No general TypeScript/Node code lens ran at all, which is the exact failure the `isLanguageGlob` guard was added to prevent.

Fix: rank by *files matched* (count the in-scope paths a skill's globs hit, which `globHits` already discards) instead of `matchedOn.length`, and cap how many kept passes may share a leading name token so one family cannot crowd out the rest of the stack.

finalFindings.title: syncPacks duplicates ensurePacks' clone block and drops its partial-clone cleanup
finalFindings.body:
The clone sequence (safety guard → `mkdirSync` → build `clone --depth 1 --single-branch [--branch ref]` → `rev-parse --verify HEAD`) exists verbatim in both `ensurePacks` (lines 181-192) and here, but only `ensurePacks` has the `rmSync` cleanup in its catch.

Failure: `packs sync` is interrupted or the `rev-parse --verify HEAD` guard throws on a commit-less clone. `syncPacks` reports the failure and leaves the directory behind; every later `packs sync` then takes the `!isGitCheckout(dir)` branch and fails with "exists but is not a git checkout", and every review warns the same, until the user deletes it by hand. The comment at line 191 shows this case was anticipated — the cleanup just did not get copied along with the code.

Extract one `clonePack(pack, dir, git)` helper carrying the guard, the argv, the verify, and the cleanup-on-throw, and call it from both paths.

finalFindings.title: A baseline skill inside an index-mode pack is silently dropped and never reported as missing
finalFindings.body:
`mode === 'index'` short-circuits to `indexSkills` before the `baselineSet.has(s.name)` check, so a baseline configured on an index pack never dispatches. `missingBaseline` (line 251) only tests membership in `packNames`, which index skills are in — so nothing warns either.

Concrete case: a user copies the shipped `anthropic-cybersecurity` entry (`mode: index`) and adds `baseline: ['secure-coding']`. The pass never runs and no output mentions it, which breaks the invariant this PR documents — "a pointer that no longer resolves surfaces as a `missingBaseline` warning" — for a pointer that resolves but can never fire.

Cheapest fix: in `missingBaseline`, also report baselines whose skill was found in an `index` pack ("baseline X is in an index-only pack and will never run"), or reject `baseline` + `mode: index` in `normalizePack` at config load.

finalFindings.title: skillsFiles mixes pass names with the reserved keys 'all' and 'project'
finalFindings.body:
`skillsFiles[p.name]` shares one map with `skillsFiles['all']` and `skillsFiles['project']`, which are written after the pass loop. Repo skills keep their plain name (only pack skills are `<pack>/<skill>`), so a repo skill at `.claude/skills/all/SKILL.md` — or `project/SKILL.md` in the no-packs fallback where project skills become passes — silently loses its own file: line 562's `ctx.skillsFiles[p.name]!` then hands that pass the union/project file, and it applies the wrong rules under its own reviewer name.

Simpler and collision-proof: keep only pass files in the map and put the two singletons on `SessionContext` as typed fields (`unionPath?`, `projectPath?`). That also removes the stringly-typed lookups at `review.ts:770` and line 540.

finalFindings.title: runDoctor dynamic-imports node:fs and re-evaluates its probes twice
finalFindings.body:
Every other dependency in this file is a static top-level import; these four `await import(...)` calls buy nothing (the packs block runs unconditionally on every `doctor` invocation) and make the function harder to read. `gitAvailable()` is then called twice on line 72 and `existsSync(linguistCachePath())` twice more at lines 90-92.

Move the four imports to the top of the file and hoist the two probes into `const git = gitAvailable()` / `const linguistCached = existsSync(linguistCachePath())`.

finalFindings.title: loadConfig home ternary repeated four times in packs.ts
finalFindings.body: `loadConfig(opts.home ? { homeOverride: opts.home } : {})` appears in `packsList`, `packsSync`, `packsAdd`, and `packsSuggest`. `loadConfig` already does `opts.homeOverride ?? homedir()` (config.ts:274), so `loadConfig({ homeOverride: opts.home })` is identical for `undefined` — drop the ternary in all four places.

finalFindings.title: skills-all.md is documented as read by codex/companions/verifier, but nothing reads it when project skills exist
finalFindings.body:
`renderUnionFile`'s doc says the union file is "read by codex, companions, and the verifier", and the same claim is repeated at `src/dispatch/single-session.ts:178` (`skillsFiles` doc) and in six docs this PR touches: `AGENTS.md:22`, `.claude/skills/debug-review-run.md:16`, `README.md:163`, `skills/help/reference/architecture.md:36`, `companion-plugins.md:40`, `reviewers-vs-skills.md:49-50`.

The wiring says otherwise. `single-session.ts:540` computes `authoritativeSkills = ctx.skillsFiles['project'] ?? unionSkills` and feeds that to companions (line 549) and the verifier (line 616); `src/commands/review.ts:770` passes the same `skillsFiles['project'] ?? skillsFiles['all']` to codex; and the pass prompts (line 562) pass only `skillsFiles['project']`. Meanwhile the union file is written unconditionally whenever `passes.length > 0`.

So on any repo with matched project skills — the normal case, and the case in this very run, where every dispatched prompt points at `skills-project.md` — `skills-all.md` is generated and read by nobody. A maintainer debugging "why did codex not see the OWASP skill" will open the wrong artifact, which is exactly what `debug-review-run.md` sends them to do.

Fix: reword to what line 540 actually implements — "the FALLBACK context for codex/companions/verifier; `skills-project.md` wins when any project skill matched" — and correct the same sentence at line 178 plus the six doc echoes. Alternatively, if the union really is meant to reach those readers, append it alongside the project file instead of being displaced by it.

finalFindings.title: `includeCodex` doc describes a behaviour this module does not have (and the field is never read)
finalFindings.body:
`/** When the Codex sibling reviewer will run, it reads the union skills file too. */` documents a conditional that does not exist here: `opts.includeCodex` is declared on line 61 and referenced nowhere else in `src/` (only `review.ts:673` passes it in). The union file's creation is gated on `passes.length > 0` (lines 461-466), not on codex; and codex's skills path is chosen in `review.ts:770`, outside this module.

The result is a dead option whose only documentation asserts a cause-and-effect relationship that no code implements — the worst kind of comment, because it reads as a design constraint and will be defended in a future refactor.

Fix: delete the field and its comment (and the `includeCodex` argument at `review.ts:673`); or, if gating the union file on codex is the intent, implement it and keep the comment.

finalFindings.title: Union-budget comment cites `MAX_PASSES`, a constant from another module that means something else
finalFindings.body:
The comment reads "The union file (codex/companions/verifier) concatenates up to MAX_PASSES bodies, so it gets a larger budget." The ceiling that actually bounds `renderUnionFile` is `MAX_TOTAL_PASSES = 16`, declared eight lines below (line 93) and applied at line 432 (`afterTriage.slice(0, MAX_TOTAL_PASSES)`).

`MAX_PASSES` is a *different* constant in a *different* module: `src/dispatch/pass-select.ts:16`, value 10, documented there as "Fallback cap when project skills ARE the passes (no packs configured)". It never bounds the union.

Failure scenario: someone tuning `UNION_FILE_CAP` greps `MAX_PASSES`, finds 10, and sizes the budget for 10 bodies while 16 can arrive — silent truncation of the last passes' skill bodies (the code warns, but the sizing decision was already made on a false premise).

Fix: change `MAX_PASSES` to `MAX_TOTAL_PASSES` in this comment.

finalFindings.title: "10-pass cap" is not any cap in the code — and this file is injected into every review pass
finalFindings.body:
This added line tells a debugger that a skill missing from the pass table may have overflowed "the 10-pass cap". There is no 10-pass cap. The caps are `MAX_STACK_PASSES = 6` (`src/dispatch/pass-select.ts:14`, stack passes only) and `MAX_TOTAL_PASSES = 16` (`src/dispatch/single-session.ts:93`, hard ceiling); baselines ride on top of the 6 and are never trimmed to 10.

This is worse than an ordinary stale doc: `.claude/skills/` files are repo skills, so every matched one is rendered into `skills-project.md` and injected into EVERY dispatched pass as authoritative project rules — this file is in the current run's `skills-project.md`. The wrong number is being handed to reviewers as fact.

It also contradicts line 17 of this same file ("overflow past the pass cap") and `.claude/skills/add-pack.md:47`, which both get it right.

Fix: "overflow past the stack-pass cap (`MAX_STACK_PASSES` = 6; baselines ride on top)".

finalFindings.title: "At most 10 passes dispatch per review" contradicts both the code and the sibling reference page
finalFindings.body:
Added line: "At most 10 passes dispatch per review; overflow joins the index." The actual selection is up to 6 stack passes (`MAX_STACK_PASSES`, `src/dispatch/pass-select.ts:14`) PLUS every baseline pointer (7 with the shipped `DEFAULT_PACKS`), hard-capped at `MAX_TOTAL_PASSES = 16` (`src/dispatch/single-session.ts:93`).

`skills/help/reference/reviewers-vs-skills.md:33`, added in this same PR, states it correctly: "at most `MAX_STACK_PASSES = 6` stack passes dispatch; baselines ride on top (typically 7, so <=13 passes)". Two user-facing help pages now give incompatible numbers, and this one is the page a user reads while deciding how many skills to write.

Fix: replace with the 6-stack + baselines wording (or defer to reviewers-vs-skills.md rather than restating a number that must now be kept in sync in two places).

finalFindings.title: "validate before caching" claims a check `parseLinguist` does not perform
finalFindings.body:
The trailing comment on `const index = parseLinguist(text); // validate before caching` implies bad content is rejected before `writeFileSync`. `parseLinguist` only throws on a YAML *syntax* error: any body that parses to a non-object falls through the `if (doc && typeof doc === 'object')` guard at lines 43-56 and returns a structurally valid but EMPTY index, which is then cached.

Failure scenario: a proxy or captive portal answers 200 with an HTML page, or the response is truncated mid-file. The empty/partial index is written to `~/.pr-review/cache/linguist-languages.yml`; from then on the cached-first branch (lines 88-91) returns it forever, because `readCache()` is non-null whenever the file parses. Language tags silently stay empty (or partial) on every subsequent review — including after `packs sync`, which only force-refreshes, and falls back to this same cache when the refresh fails. Stack detection degrades with no warning, which is precisely the failure this comment promises to prevent.

Fix: make the comment true rather than deleting the check — `if (index.byExt.size === 0) throw new Error('unusable languages.yml');` before writing the cache, and treat an empty cached index as a cache miss at line 90.

finalFindings.title: "mirrors loadSkillFile naming" is false for any pack file that declares a frontmatter `name:`
finalFindings.body:
`skillNameOf` derives the name from the pack-relative path alone. `loadSkillFile` does not: `src/plugins/builtin.ts:119,126` computes `normalizeSkillName(declaredName ?? inferNameFromPath(filePath))`, so a frontmatter `name:` wins over the filename. The two "mirror" each other only while every pack file's frontmatter agrees with its directory name.

The divergence is not cosmetic — `skillNameOf` exists solely to power the exclude-by-name half of `listPackFiles` (line 46), and that is the control keeping operational/offensive SecOps skills out of review context (`DEFAULT_PACKS.anthropic-cybersecurity.exclude` in `src/config.ts`). A pack file at `skills/generic-helper/SKILL.md` with `name: hunting-lateral-movement` loads under the excluded name but is matched against `generic-helper`, so the exclude misses and the skill lands in the index. It fails silently and in the permissive direction. (The three shipped packs happen to agree today — I checked — which is why this will not surface until a pack changes upstream.)

Fix: state the limitation ("path-derived name; a frontmatter `name:` is NOT consulted, so exclude-by-name is best-effort"), or read the frontmatter name here so the mirror is real.

finalFindings.title: `matchedOn` doc omits the 'glob' rows that carry no globs, and the triage comment inherits the error
finalFindings.body:
The doc says `matchedOn` is "the matching globs (glob) or stack tags (tag); [] for repo/forced/baseline" — enumerating exactly which labels yield an empty array. But line 186 pushes untargeted project skills as `candidate(s, 'glob', [])`: matchedBy 'glob' with zero globs, because "empty applies_to = always applies".

Two things the comment hides:
- The `## Passes` / `## Skills` tables render `glob | —` for a skill that matched no file at all, which reads as a bug to anyone using the table to debug routing.
- `triagePasses` in `src/dispatch/single-session.ts:184` is commented "Docs-only PRs run only passes pinned to files (glob) or forced" and filters on `matchedBy === 'glob'`. An untargeted project skill is not pinned to files, yet survives docs-only triage. Whether or not that is desired, both comments currently describe a rule the code does not implement.

Fix: either document the third case here ("…or [] when an untargeted project skill always applies") and reword the triage comment, or give always-applies project skills a distinct label so 'glob' keeps its stated meaning.

finalFindings.title: Comment justifies skipping Linguist on a premise that misses its second consumer
finalFindings.body:
"No packs configured → language tags feed nothing glob/tag-matched" is true for pass selection, but the tags have a second consumer the comment does not mention: `selection.stackTags` is written into `pr-context.md`'s `## Stack` block (`src/dispatch/single-session.ts:248`), which every dispatched pass reads as the PR's stack description.

With `skill_packs: []` — the documented fallback where project skills become the passes — that block silently degrades to manifest/ecosystem tags with no languages, and nothing in the run reports why. The comment as written tells the next maintainer the skip is free.

Fix: name the tradeoff ("…and the `## Stack` block in pr-context.md degrades to manifest tags only"), or keep the load when it costs nothing: `config.skillPacks.length > 0 || existsSync(linguistCachePath(opts.homeOverride))`.

finalFindings.title: "The generic subagent type both runtimes accept" is asserted as fact but verified on one runtime
finalFindings.body:
This PR's own description states the Copilot runtime could not be exercised: "Declared not-verifiable here: Copilot runtime (binary not on PATH — `GENERIC_AGENT` is the single line to adjust if its generic agent type differs)". The comment states cross-runtime acceptance flatly, so the one place recording the uncertainty is the PR body — which disappears the moment the PR merges, while the comment stays and reads as settled.

Failure scenario: a Copilot run returns zero findings because `task(agent_type: 'general-purpose')` is rejected; the maintainer reads this comment, concludes the agent type is fine, and looks elsewhere.

Fix: keep the fact, drop the certainty — "'general-purpose' is Claude Code's built-in generic subagent type; assumed compatible with Copilot's `task` tool but not yet verified against it — this is the single line to change if Copilot names it differently."

finalFindings.title: Transitional comment ("until the loader drops it") on a dead stub with no removal trigger
finalFindings.body:
`loadBuiltInReviewers()` now returns `[]`, and its comment ends "Kept only until the loader drops it." That is a snapshot of an in-progress refactor: no issue, no date, no owner, and no way for a future reader to tell whether the moment has passed. Comments describing a transitional state rot fastest, and this one will outlive everyone's memory of the 0.7.0 migration.

The event it waits for is one line away in this same PR: `src/plugins/loader.ts:184` is the sole caller, inside `if (includeBuiltIn && !skillsOnly)`, and the review path always passes `skillsOnly: true`.

Fix: delete the function and the `includeBuiltIn` branch now (the diff is three lines), or keep the function and replace the comment with the durable fact alone — "There are no built-in reviewers: every review pass is a skill selected at review time" — with no forward-looking clause.

finalFindings.title: No test covers a baseline that also stack-matches but loses the MAX_STACK_PASSES cap — the "baselines always dispatch" invariant silently breaks
finalFindings.body:
`selectPasses` promises that every baseline runs (`tests/pass-select.test.ts` even asserts *"baselines can no longer be starved out"*), but the guarantee only holds for baselines that match **nothing else**.

A baseline skill that ALSO hits a glob/tag gets pushed as a `glob`/`tag` candidate and `continue`s before the `baselineSet.has(s.name)` branch ever runs. It is therefore absent from `candidates.filter((c) => c.pass.matchedBy === 'baseline')` here. If it then lands outside `stackCandidates.slice(0, MAX_STACK_PASSES)`, it goes to `stackOverflow` → the on-demand index and is **never dispatched at all**.

Failure scenario: a pack configures `baseline: ['nodejs-security']` (the documented per-pack baseline pattern) and that skill has `tags: [node]`. On a Node PR with 6+ other stack-matching skills, `nodejs-security` sorts below the cap → dropped to the index, no warning, `missingBaseline` empty. Every review of that repo silently loses its declared baseline lens.

The existing dedupe test (`baseline dedupe keeps the higher tier`) only exercises the case where the dual-matched baseline is *inside* the cap, so it gives false confidence.

Suggested test: build `MAX_STACK_PASSES + 2` glob candidates where one of them is named in `baseline`, and assert it is still present in `sel.passes` (not in `indexEntries`).

finalFindings.title: The symlink-containment guard on pack files has zero test coverage
finalFindings.body:
`containedIn` is the only thing stopping a third-party pack (arbitrary git repos cloned from user config, read by agents with tool access) from pulling arbitrary local files into agent context via a symlink — the comment on it says exactly that. Yet no test in `tests/packs-load.test.ts` ever creates a symlink inside a pack dir: the tests only cover include/exclude globs, index mode, and duplicate names.

Failure scenario: delete the `.filter((rel) => containedIn(...))` line (or invert the `catch { return false }` to `true`, or break the `base + '/'` prefix check on POSIX after a Windows-only edit) and the entire suite stays green. A pack containing `skills/leak/SKILL.md -> ~/.ssh/id_rsa` or `-> ~/.aws/credentials` would then be loaded as a skill body and shipped into `pass-*.md` / `skills-index.md`, i.e. into every dispatched agent's context.

Suggested test: in a temp pack dir, `symlinkSync` an outside `.md` file into an included path and assert `listPackFiles` excludes it while a real file at the same path is included. Wrap symlink creation in try/catch and `skip` when it throws — CI runs `windows-latest`, where unprivileged symlink creation can fail.

finalFindings.title: A baseline pointing at an index-mode pack skill is neither dispatched nor reported as missing — untested
finalFindings.body:
`missingBaseline` is computed from `packNames`, which includes skills from `mode: 'index'` packs. But index skills `continue` out of the loop before the `baselineSet.has(s.name)` branch, so they can never become a baseline candidate.

Net effect: for a pack configured with `mode: index` and a non-empty `baseline: [...]` (both are documented, independently settable yaml keys), the baseline skill never runs as a pass AND produces no `missingBaseline` warning — the exact silent rot the repo rules say baseline pointers must never have ("break loudly, not silently").

No test covers this combination: `index-only packs never become passes; missing baseline reported` uses a baseline name that is absent from the pack entirely, which takes the other branch.

Suggested test: one pack with `mode: 'index'` whose skill name IS in `baseline`, asserting either that it dispatches or that it lands in `missingBaseline` — pick the intended contract and pin it (reporting it as missing, or rejecting the config at load time, is the cheaper fix).

finalFindings.title: Changed pack `git:` source is untested and unguarded — the old checkout is silently reused and pulled
finalFindings.body:
`syncPacks` carefully guards a changed `ref:` (with a test: `a changed ref: is reported, never silently pulled from the old branch`), but the identical hazard for a changed `git:` has neither guard nor test. `PackMeta` already persists `git`, and nothing ever compares it.

Failure scenario: a user edits `skill_packs` from `- git: acme/rules-v1\n  name: rules` to `git: acme/rules-v2` keeping `name: rules`. `ensurePacks` sees the dir exists and marks it present; `syncPacks` runs `git pull --ff-only` inside the v1 checkout. Every subsequent review is performed with v1's review knowledge while `packs list` prints the pack as fresh and synced — a wrong-content review that reports as healthy. The same applies to a repo yaml that repoints a pack name inherited from the global config.

Suggested test: mirror the ref-change test — `ensurePacks` a pack from remote A, then `syncPacks` the same `name` with `git` pointing at remote B, and assert it is reported in `failed` ("source changed — delete <dir> and re-sync") rather than silently pulled.

finalFindings.title: The post-clone HEAD verification and its cleanup path are untested
finalFindings.body:
`git(['rev-parse', '--verify', 'HEAD'], dir)` exists specifically to catch a clone that produced a `.git` dir with no commit, so the catch block can `rmSync` the partial checkout. Nothing tests it: `a bad source warns and leaves no directory behind` fails at `git clone` itself, so it never reaches this line.

Why the untested branch matters: if this verification is removed or the cleanup is skipped, the empty checkout persists, and every later run takes the `existsSync(dir) && isGitCheckout(dir)` fast path — the pack is reported present and fresh while contributing zero skills forever, with no warning. That is a silent, permanent loss of review knowledge that only a manual `rm -rf` fixes.

Suggested test: `git init -b main` a remote with NO commit (clone succeeds, HEAD unborn), run `ensurePacks`, and assert `present` is empty, a `clone failed` warning is emitted, and `packDir` no longer exists.

finalFindings.title: The MAX_PASSES fallback cap (project skills as passes) is never exercised
finalFindings.body:
In the no-pack-passes fallback, `project.slice(0, MAX_PASSES)` becomes the passes and `project.slice(MAX_PASSES)` is pushed to the index. `MAX_PASSES` is exported but never imported by any test: `fallback with no pack passes: project skills become the passes themselves` uses exactly 2 project skills, so both the cap and the overflow-to-index branch are dead in the suite.

Failure scenario: a repo with `skill_packs: []` and 25 project skills (the configuration the docs recommend for teams that only want their own rules). Swap `MAX_PASSES` for `MAX_STACK_PASSES` here, or invert the slice bounds, and 15+ business-rule skills are silently demoted to the index — or 25 passes are dispatched, blowing the session token budget — with a green suite either way. This is the product's stated core value path (project rules driving the review), so it deserves a pin.

Suggested test: `MAX_PASSES + 2` targeted repo skills, `packSkills: []` — assert `passes.length === MAX_PASSES` and that the 2 overflowed skills appear in `indexEntries` with `matchedBy: 'index'` routes.

finalFindings.title: Test fixture omits the required `projectSkills`, and nothing covers the review.ts → session wiring that injects project rules
finalFindings.body:
`emptySelection()` is annotated `PassSelection` but omits the required `projectSkills` field. It compiles only because `tsconfig.json` excludes `tests/` and `tsx` strips types without checking — so the type annotation buys nothing here, and the whole-pipeline tests run with an input shape the real `selectPasses` can never return.

The consequence is a real hole, not just tidiness: `SingleSessionOptions.projectSkills` is optional (`projectSkills?`) and `prepareSessionContext` defaults it with `?? []`. So if `src/commands/review.ts` stopped forwarding `projectSkills: selection.projectSkills`, `skills-project.md` would never be written and every pass, companion and the verifier would lose the user's authoritative business rules — and all 327 tests would still pass. `session-context.test.ts` covers the downstream half by passing `projectSkills` in by hand; `pass-select.test.ts` covers the upstream half; nothing covers the seam between them.

Suggested: (1) add `projectSkills: []` to the fixture so it matches the real contract; (2) extend one `runReview` test so the injected selection returns a non-empty `projectSkills` and assert `skills-project.md` exists in the run dir and its content reaches the orchestrator prompt. Consider also adding a `tsc --noEmit` pass over `tests/` in CI so fixture drift from production types is caught.

finalFindings.title: Project-rules budget caps (PROJECT_BODY_CAP / PROJECT_FILE_CAP) have no test — the highest-value content is dropped on an untested branch
finalFindings.body:
`renderProjectFile` has two lossy branches: per-skill truncation at `PROJECT_BODY_CAP` (16k) and hard stop at `PROJECT_FILE_CAP` (64k), where the current skill *and every skill after it* are omitted with only a stderr warning. Neither is covered — `pass body cap — oversized skill is truncated` only exercises the analogous `PASS_BODY_CAP` path in `renderPassFile`.

Failure scenario: a repo with many detailed business-rule skills (the live case in the PR description mentions 10 matched project skills; another repo had 47). Once the union crosses 64k, the tail is dropped from the context that is supposed to "OVERRIDE generic judgement" — silently, per-run, with no signal in the summary. An off-by-one or a reordering of the `total` accumulation would change *which* rules survive, and no test would notice.

Suggested test: two project skills whose bodies straddle `PROJECT_FILE_CAP` — assert the first is present, the second's marker is absent, the `[omitted: ...]` sentinel is written, and the warning names the omitted skill. Same shape for `PROJECT_BODY_CAP` truncation.

finalFindings.title: The git argv-injection guards are only tested behind a `git on PATH` skip
finalFindings.body:
`isSafeGitSource` / `isSafeRef` are pure string predicates — the guard that keeps `ext::sh -c whoami` and `--upload-pack=...` out of `git clone` argv, fed from repo-controlled `.pr-review.yaml`. They are exported, but the only test that touches them (`unsafe git sources and refs are refused before reaching argv`) is gated on `{ skip }` because its fixture calls `makeRemote`, which needs git. On any machine or container without git, the security assertions vanish silently rather than failing.

Suggested test: a git-independent unit test asserting the predicates directly — `isSafeGitSource('ext::sh -c whoami') === false`, `'--upload-pack=x'` false, `'https://…'`/`'git@host:owner/repo'` true, a nonexistent local path false; `isSafeRef('--exec=whoami') === false`, `'v1.2.3'` true. That keeps the guard pinned regardless of the environment and costs no fixture setup.

finalFindings.title: firstLine() reports git's progress banner instead of the actual clone error
`// validate before caching` validates nothing — a 200-with-HTML response poisons the Linguist cache permanently and silently
finalFindings.body:
`parseLinguist(text)` cannot fail, so the comment on this line describes validation that does not exist. Verified with this repo's `yaml`:

- `parse('<html><body>404 Not Found</body></html>')` → a **string**, no throw → `doc && typeof doc === 'object'` is false → empty `byExt`/`byFilename`.
- `parse('{"error":"rate limited"}')` → an object whose single value is a string → every entry hits `typeof lang !== 'object'` → `continue` → empty index.

So any 200 response that is not `languages.yml` (captive portal, corporate proxy interstitial, CDN error page, a JSON error body) is written to `~/.pr-review/cache/linguist-languages.yml` and returned as a **truthy, empty** index. From then on:

1. `existsSync(cache)` is true, so every review reads the poisoned cache and never re-fetches.
2. `detectStack` sees `opts.linguist` non-null, so it does **not** push its `Linguist data unavailable — language tags skipped` note.
3. `languages` is empty, so no pack skill can glob/tag-match the stack, and every review silently runs baselines only — the exact failure the stack-detection feature exists to prevent, reported as a normal successful review.

Fix — validate the shape before caching, and treat an empty index as a failure so the existing fallback/warn path runs:

```ts
const index = parseLinguist(text);
if (index.byExt.size < 100) throw new Error('response is not languages.yml (parsed 0 usable languages)');
```

Also make `readCache()` reject an empty index for the same reason, so an already-poisoned cache self-heals on the next run.

finalFindings.title: `packs sync` prints "✓ Linguist languages.yml refreshed" when the refresh failed and the stale cache was silently reused
`packs add` silently destroys the user's global config when the YAML fails to parse
Pack clone failures and missing baselines degrade the review invisibly — stderr only, never the summary or the exit code
finalFindings.body:
`packsResult.warnings` (clone failed, not-a-git-checkout, git missing, >30-day staleness) and the `missingBaseline` warnings a few lines below are written to stderr and nowhere else. They never reach `pr-review-summary.md`, the posted findings, or the exit code.

Failure scenario: on a machine behind a proxy, the `owasp` pack fails to clone. `ensurePacks` pushes a warning, the review continues with the `awesome-copilot` passes only, finds 4 nits, and exits 0 with a summary whose `## Skills` table simply lists fewer passes. The security/error-handling/logging baselines never ran, and nothing in the artifact the user actually reads says so. Under `--detach` (the mode the slash command uses) stderr goes to `detached.log`, which nobody opens.

This contradicts the rule the same file enforces a few lines further down — *"Never a silent 0: an empty review is not a clean PR"* — for the partial case, which is the far more common one. A review that lost half its lenses is not a clean review either.

Fix: carry the warnings into `renderSummary` so they render above the findings, e.g.

```
## Degraded
- owasp: clone failed — fatal: unable to access ...; passes error-handling, logging did NOT run
```

and treat a missing baseline as a non-zero-exit condition (or at minimum a `⚠` line in the summary), since a baseline pointer is by definition a lens the config says must run on every PR.

finalFindings.title: Every packs-sync failure gets the same "upstream force-pushed, delete <dir>" hint — including failures where deleting is wrong or the dir doesn't exist
writeMeta swallows the metadata write failure while syncPacks still reports the pack as synced
An unreadable pack directory silently contributes zero skills — the "ensurePacks already warned" justification does not hold
One unreadable file in a 600-skill third-party pack aborts the entire review with a raw stack trace
normalizePack validates only the top-level list shape — a string `include:` crashes the review, and a typo'd `mode:` silently flips an index pack into dispatched passes
The MAX_TOTAL_PASSES trim drops passes into the index with no warning, unlike every other truncation in this file
Unreadable/unparseable manifests silently yield no dependency tags, even though StackInfo.notes exists to report exactly this
finalFindings.body:
Three catches in this file drop dependency detection on the floor with no record: `jsonDeps` (line 49, `// unparseable manifest → no tags from it`), the `findManifests` walk (line 122, bare `return`), and this one (`// unreadable manifest → skip`).

`readDependencyTags` returns `{ dependencies, ecosystems, manifests }` and `detectStack` already has a `notes: string[]` channel that is printed to stderr *and* rendered into the `--context-only` `## Stack` block — but a failed manifest read never populates it.

Failure scenario: a repo's `package.json` contains a trailing comma (or is a jsonc-style file, or is a 0-byte artifact of an interrupted checkout). `jsonDeps` returns `[]`, so no dependency tags exist, so no framework skill can tag-match, so the review runs baselines only. `--context-only` prints `- **Dependencies:** (none)` — indistinguishable from a repo that genuinely has no dependencies. Debugging "why did the nestjs pass stop running?" means reading source, because nothing anywhere mentions the manifest.

Hidden errors here: EACCES, EISDIR, ENOENT (a race with a checkout), and any `JSON.parse` SyntaxError in `jsonDeps`.

Fix: thread a `notes` array (or return the failures) so `detectStack` can push e.g. `package.json is not valid JSON (Unexpected token } at position 412) — dependency tags from it skipped`.

finalFindings.title: Eval harness passes vacuously when a fixture's must_find is missing or misspelled
"Baselines ALWAYS dispatch" is not guaranteed — a baseline that also stack-matches can be pushed past the cap into the index
finalFindings.body:
The loop above classifies each pack skill with `continue` after the first hit, so a skill that glob- or tag-matches is recorded as `matchedBy: 'glob' | 'tag'` and **never** reaches the `baselineSet.has(s.name)` branch. It therefore lands in `stackCandidates`, is subject to `slice(0, MAX_STACK_PASSES)`, and can end up in `stackOverflow` → the on-demand index. The `baselines` filter here only rescues candidates already labelled `'baseline'`, so it cannot recover it.

Failure scenario: a user sets `baseline: ['typescript-best-practices']` on a pack (or upstream adds tags to an existing baseline skill). On a TypeScript PR that skill now tag-matches, sorts below the six glob hits, overflows, and silently does not run — while `passes.json` records it as `index`, so the summary reports it as "available on demand", not as "your configured baseline was dropped". `missingBaseline` also cannot catch it, since the skill did load.

Same class: a `baseline:` entry inside a `mode: 'index'` pack is skipped at the top of the loop and is *not* reported by `missingBaseline` (it is in `packNames`), so that contradictory config is a silent no-op too.

Fix: resolve baselines before the cap — e.g. mark `isBaseline` on the candidate regardless of how it matched, and exclude baseline candidates from `stackOverflow`.

finalFindings.title: Failed cleanup of a partial clone leaves a directory that the next run treats as a healthy pack, not as "not a git checkout"
SkillPack allows mode:'index' with a non-empty baseline — a contradictory state that silently does nothing
finalFindings.body:
`SkillPack` makes `mode: 'auto' | 'index'` and `baseline: string[]` independent, so `{ mode: 'index', baseline: ['x'] }` is representable and means two contradictory things: "never dispatch as a pass" and "dispatch on every PR". Nothing rejects it, and the silence is total:

- `src/commands/review.ts:650` qualifies baselines from **every** pack: `config.skillPacks.flatMap((p) => p.baseline.map((b) => `${p.name}/${b}`))` — no `mode` filter.
- `selectPasses` pushes index-mode skills to `indexSkills` and `continue`s before the `baselineSet` check, so the pointer can never match.
- `missingBaseline` is computed against `packNames = new Set(input.packSkills.map((s) => s.name))`, which **includes** index-mode skills — so the unreachable baseline is not reported as missing either.

A user who sets `mode: index` on a pack while keeping its `baseline:` list gets a review with a silently absent lens and zero diagnostics — the exact rot the missing-baseline warning exists to prevent.

Two cheap fixes, either works: (a) in `normalizePack` (src/config.ts), warn and force `baseline: []` when `mode === 'index'`, making the state unrepresentable past the config boundary; or (b) compute `missingBaseline` against dispatchable skills only (`input.packSkills.filter((s) => s.mode !== 'index')`) so the pointer breaks loudly, consistent with the stated "pointers, not content — they break loudly, not silently" contract.

finalFindings.title: PackMeta records `git` but syncPacks never verifies it — changing a pack's URL pulls the old repo and relabels it as the new one
PassSelection.routes is dead — the shipped routing is a second, divergent computation in single-session.ts
finalFindings.body:
`PassSelection.routes` has no production consumer. `review.ts` reads only `passes`, `projectSkills`, `indexEntries`, `stackTags`, and `missingBaseline`; the `passes.json` that AGENTS.md and the debug-review-run skill document as the routing record is built independently at `src/dispatch/single-session.ts:479`, from post-skip/post-triage/post-`MAX_TOTAL_PASSES` state. The two disagree by construction: only the single-session one can emit `'skipped'` rows, and only it reflects the second cap.

The cost is not just dead code — `tests/pass-select.test.ts` asserts against `sel.routes` (lines 135, 181, 219-224), so the routing invariant is unit-tested on the copy that never ships, while the copy users actually read has no equivalent coverage. Any future change to routing semantics will be made green by tests that prove nothing about the artifact.

Fix: delete `routes` from `PassSelection` (and the `PassRoute` rows built at line 244) and move those assertions onto `prepareSessionContext`'s `routing`, so there is one definition of the routing record.

finalFindings.title: SkillDefinition encodes one fact in three independent optional fields (pack/origin/mode)
finalFindings.body:
`pack?: string`, `origin?: 'repo' | 'home' | 'plugin' | 'forced' | 'pack'`, and `mode?: 'auto' | 'index'` all describe pack membership but vary independently, so the type admits states no producer creates and no consumer expects: `{ origin: 'pack', pack: undefined }`, `{ origin: 'repo', mode: 'index' }`, `{ pack: 'owasp', origin: 'repo' }`. Only `loadPackSkills` sets the trio coherently; the type does not require it.

The defensive code this forces is already visible — `tokensOf` writes `s.pack && s.name.startsWith(`${s.pack}/`)` because it cannot trust that `pack` is set whenever the name is prefixed — and `mode` is only ever honoured inside the `input.packSkills` loop, so a skill carrying `mode: 'index'` on any other path would be dispatched as a pass. (Not reachable today only because `loadSkillFile` doesn't parse `mode` from frontmatter — an accident, not an invariant.)

Small, non-breaking fix that makes the illegal states unrepresentable: replace the three with one optional group, `pack?: { name: string; mode: 'auto' | 'index' }`, and keep `origin` for the non-pack provenance the loader tags via `withOrigin`. Presence of `pack` then *is* pack-ness, and `mode` cannot exist without it.

finalFindings.title: Two definitions of "the skill name" — exclude globs match the path-derived name, not the name the skill loads under
finalFindings.body:
`listPackFiles` matches `exclude` against `skillNameOf(rel)`, which derives the name from the path alone. The name the skill actually loads under comes from `loadSkillFile`, which prefers frontmatter: `normalizeSkillName(declaredName ?? inferNameFromPath(filePath))`. The doc comment above ("exclude also matches the normalized skill name (so `hunting-*` excludes `skills/hunting-x/SKILL.md`)") describes the loaded name, but the code cannot see it — `skillNameOf` is a hand-rolled mirror of naming logic that lives in another module.

Today the mirror happens to agree (in `anthropic-cybersecurity` every `SKILL.md` frontmatter `name:` equals its directory name), so the curated exclude list works. It is one upstream file with a mismatched `name:` away from not working: a skill in `skills/red-team-ops/SKILL.md` declaring `name: hunting-c2` is loaded and named `hunting-c2` while `hunting-*` never matches it — the operational-verb curation this PR's DEFAULT_PACKS entry depends on silently leaks.

Fix: derive the name from the loaded definition rather than mirroring the rule — load first, then apply the name-based excludes against `def.name` in `loadPackSkills` (path-based excludes can stay in `listPackFiles`). That removes the second naming implementation entirely.

finalFindings.title: StackInfo.tags is denormalized with no field to reconstruct it from
finalFindings.body:
`tags` is documented as `languages ∪ dependencies ∪ manifest-ecosystem tags`, but `ecosystems` is not a field of `StackInfo` — it is computed locally at line 76 and folded into `tags` at line 91, then discarded. The stated invariant is therefore not checkable by any consumer, and the third input is unobservable.

This has a concrete debugging cost: `--context-only` (src/commands/review.ts) prints `stack.languages` and `stack.dependencies` as the explanation of the `## Stack` block, and pass selection matches skill tokens against `stack.tags`. An ecosystem-only tag (`nodejs`, `nuget`, `bundler` — exactly the ones the `ecosystemTags` comment says exist so OWASP's Nodejs/DotNet sheets can tag-match) can be the sole reason a pass ran, yet appears in no printed field. The preview says "why did this pass match" and the answer is not there.

Fix: add `ecosystems: string[]` to `StackInfo`, return it from `detectStack`, and print it alongside languages/dependencies — `tags` then becomes a derivable convenience rather than an opaque third source.

finalFindings.title: A baseline pass that also stack-matches is silently evicted by MAX_STACK_PASSES — the exact starvation this PR claims to fix
finalFindings.body:
`selectPasses` reaches the baseline check only after the glob/tag branches have already `continue`d, so a baseline whose own name token overlaps a stack tag is labelled `matchedBy: 'tag'` instead of `'baseline'`:

https://github.com/guimatheus92/pr-review/blob/b61dbdaead3509b00cc2c8a2c1c909ce46d6561a/src/dispatch/pass-select.ts#L161-L170

It then sorts below every glob hit, and once 6 glob candidates outrank it, it falls into `stackOverflow` — which is never added back to `kept`:

https://github.com/guimatheus92/pr-review/blob/b61dbdaead3509b00cc2c8a2c1c909ce46d6561a/src/dispatch/pass-select.ts#L206-L218

`candidates.filter(c => c.pass.matchedBy === 'baseline')` never sees it, so the baseline is dropped from the passes and appears only in `indexEntries`. `missingBaseline` stays empty (line 251 only checks that the skill loaded), so **nothing warns**.

Reproduced against the real synced default packs, the real cached Linguist index, and a real `go.mod` containing `cloud.google.com/go/logging v1.11.0` (a common Go dependency, which yields stack tag `logging`):

```
passes:
  awesome-copilot/power-apps-canvas-yaml [glob]
  awesome-copilot/containerization-docker-best-practices [glob]
  awesome-copilot/github-copilot-sdk-go [glob]
  awesome-copilot/go [glob]
  awesome-copilot/go-mcp-server [glob]
  awesome-copilot/kubernetes-manifests [glob]
  awesome-copilot/code-review-generic [baseline]
  ... (5 more baselines)

missingBaseline warning: []
BASELINES THAT RESOLVED BUT DID NOT DISPATCH: [ 'owasp/logging' ]
  demoted to on-demand index? true
```

The failure mode is adverse-selected: the baseline most likely to collide with a stack tag is the one whose topic matches the repo, so the *most* relevant baseline is the one silently lost.

This contradicts the code's own comment ("Baselines ALWAYS dispatch"), the test message at `tests/pass-select.test.ts:127` ("baselines can no longer be starved out"), and AGENTS.md: *"passes = pack glob/tag (cap `MAX_STACK_PASSES=6`; extension-only globs need stack-consistent name/tags) + EVERY baseline"*.

The existing coverage misses it: `tests/pass-select.test.ts:161` ("baseline dedupe keeps the higher tier") exercises a dual-matched baseline only *under* the cap.

Fix is small — after slicing, promote any `stackOverflow` candidate whose name is in `baselineSet` back into `kept` (or check `baselineSet.has(s.name)` before the glob/tag branches and keep the higher tier only when it survives the cap).

finalFindings.title: PR adds .claude/commands/fix.md, a 22 KB command hardcoded to an unrelated private project and pointing at a CLI that does not exist in this repo
finalFindings.body:
This PR adds a new 265-line `.claude/commands/fix.md` that has nothing to do with the change (or with this repo). It is hardcoded to a different, private codebase:

https://github.com/guimatheus92/pr-review/blob/b61dbdaead3509b00cc2c8a2c1c909ce46d6561a/.claude/commands/fix.md#L49-L52

```bash
ROOT="$(pwd | grep -o '.*PrecoPratico')"
CLI_DIR="$ROOT/PrecoPratico-Docs/tools/cli"
CLI="$CLI_DIR/dist/fix.js"
```

There is no `tools/` directory in this repo, so the command is dead on arrival here. It also carries stack- and project-specific content that this repo deliberately keeps out of itself — NestJS decorators (line 126) and `PrecoPratico-Docs/.claude/skills/...` routing targets including `pp-*`, `render-guide`, `types-guide` (line 212).

It looks like an accidental commit of a personal `~/.claude/commands/fix.md` into a public, redistributable plugin repo, swept up by the `feat!: zero built-in reviewers` commit (`bab134a`). It should be dropped from the PR.

finalFindings.title: Docs-only triage can now drop every pass — the pre-0.7 "never triage down to zero" guard was removed, so a docs PR can exit 0 as "clean"
finalFindings.body:
`triagePasses` (src/dispatch/single-session.ts:185-190) keeps only passes whose `matchedBy` is `glob` or `forced` on a docs-only PR. The function it replaces (`triageReviewers` on main) had an explicit escape hatch that this rewrite dropped:

```ts
if (surviving.length === 0) {
  // e.g. the surviving reviewer was --skip'ed: never triage down to zero.
  return { dispatch: shorts, skipped: [] };
}
```

Without it the pipeline can now triage a real review down to nothing, and `src/commands/review.ts:727-734` turns that into `exitCode 0` with the summary "docs-only PR with no doc-scoped review skill — nothing to review". A caller (and `--fail-on high` in CI) cannot distinguish that from "reviewed and clean".

Why no single pass caught it — the trigger spans four files, and each pass only saw one:
- `src/stack/linguist.ts:101-111` returns `null` on a cold cache + failed download (stderr warning only), so `stackTags` carries no language tags.
- `src/dispatch/pass-select.ts:151-165` gates bare extension globs (`**/*.md`, which is what the pack's markdown skills declare) on a tag overlap. No `markdown`/`md` tag ⇒ those skills fall to the index and the only surviving passes are `baseline` ones.
- `triagePasses` then drops every `baseline` pass.
- The lenses-vs-context change means the user's own matched skills are `projectSkills`, never passes — so unlike 0.6 they cannot survive triage either. `skills-project.md` is written and read by nobody.

Net effect: on a docs-only PR with a cold/failed Linguist cache, a repo whose own `.claude/skills` rules explicitly target `**/*.md` gets a silent zero-finding exit 0. The tested behaviour (tests/zero-passes.test.ts:119, tests/session-context.test.ts:170) locks the new shape in, so this is a deliberate-looking hole rather than an obvious bug.

Fix: restore the never-zero guard in `triagePasses` (when `surviving.length === 0`, dispatch the untriaged set), or — if the triage-to-zero outcome is intended — make it loud rather than exit 0 when `projectSkills.length > 0` (the repo has matched rules that produced no review) and say so in the summary, not just stderr.

finalFindings.title: cwd is identity-checked before reading manifests but not before loading project skills — an unrelated repo's rules inject as authoritative into every pass
finalFindings.body:
This PR introduces `cwdMatchesPr` (src/stack/detect.ts:21-28, 77-88) precisely because "the checkout may not be the PR's repo", and refuses to read dependency manifests when it is not. The very next statement in the same function, `loadAll({ cwd, config, skillsOnly: true, home })` at src/commands/review.ts:635, applies no such guard: `autodiscoveryPaths` (src/config.ts:321-326) reads `<cwd>/.claude|.copilot|.github|.agents/skills` unconditionally.

That mismatch existed before, but this PR multiplies its blast radius. In 0.6 a matched repo skill was one pass among many. In 0.7 `selectPasses` routes every matched project skill into `skills-project.md` (src/dispatch/pass-select.ts:173-196), and `prepareSessionContext` wires that file into EVERY dispatched pass (`passTaskPrompt`), every companion agent (single-session.ts:549), the verifier (single-session.ts:616) and the Codex sibling (review.ts:770) with the wording "authoritative and OVERRIDE generic judgement".

Concrete failure: a maintainer sitting in repo A runs `/pr-review <url-of-repo-B-PR>` (the slash command imposes no cwd requirement). Repo A's business rules are injected as authoritative into every pass reviewing repo B's diff, the stack notes correctly say "cwd is not a checkout of B", and the resulting mis-grounded findings are posted as inline threads on B's PR. Nothing in the summary tells the reader whose rules were applied.

Each pass missed it because detect.ts and loader.ts were reviewed separately; the contradiction only shows when you put the new guard next to the unguarded consumer two lines away.

Fix: reuse the guard. Compute the origin once in `runReview`, and when `cwdMatchesPr(origin, ref.owner, ref.repo)` is false either skip `paths.repoSkills` or demote them to the on-demand index, with a note in the summary — the same treatment dependency tags already get.

finalFindings.title: Stack detection never looks at the PR's own diff — the PR that adds a framework gets no pass for that framework
finalFindings.body:
`detectStack` derives dependency and ecosystem tags exclusively from files on disk (`readDependencyTags(root)` → `findManifests` + `readFileSync`, src/stack/detect.ts:80-83, src/stack/manifests.ts:126-139). The gather already holds the new-side patch for every changed `package.json` / `pyproject.toml` / `go.mod`, and `isManifest` + `parseManifest` already take a basename and text — the diff is simply never fed to them.

Three consequences, all invisible in a local test run:
1. A PR that *introduces* a dependency (the PR that most needs that pack's skill) contributes no tag for it, because the reviewer's working tree predates the change.
2. Tag output depends on which branch the reviewer happens to have checked out, which contradicts the module contract one layer up — src/dispatch/pass-select.ts:5-9 calls itself "Deterministic selection of the review passes for one PR".
3. When cwd is not the PR's repo at all, `dependencies` and `ecosystems` are always empty, leaving only Linguist language tags. Because `pass-select.ts:151-165` gates bare extension globs on a tag overlap, stack passes then collapse toward zero while the run still reports success — the degradation reaches only `stack.notes` on stderr (review.ts:642), never the summary.

Missed by the other passes because manifests.ts was reviewed for I/O error handling and detect.ts for credential logging; nobody compared the tag source against the diff the passes are selected for.

Fix: parse the new-side content of changed manifests out of `gather.changedFiles[].patch` through the existing `parseManifest`/`ecosystemTags`, union it with the cwd result, and record in `StackInfo.notes` (and in the rendered summary) when the cwd contribution was skipped.

finalFindings.title: The "zero reviewers" migration is only half-applied to the user-facing surface — `configure` still collects reviewer dirs, and the new comment misstates forced-skill routing
finalFindings.body:
This PR removes `agents/` and updates `.pr-review.example.yaml:44-47` to state that the `extra_reviewers*` keys "still parse but are ignored on the review path". It also fixed `runConfigureQuick` to write `extra_skills_dirs` instead of `extra_reviewers_dirs` (src/commands/configure.ts:32-45). The same fix was not carried across the rest of the surface:

- `runConfigureInteractive` (src/commands/configure.ts:57-62) still asks "Extra reviewers dirs (comma-separated)" as its second question and writes the answer to `extra_reviewers_dirs`. The tool's own setup wizard therefore collects the user's review criteria into a key its own example config documents as dead — the user gets no warning and no findings.
- `src/cli.ts:51-52` still advertises `--reviewer <path...>` "Include a specific .md file as a reviewer" and `--reviewers-dir`, while `loadAll({ skillsOnly: true })` (src/plugins/loader.ts:220-225) skips `config.reviewers`/`reviewersDirs` entirely. Neighbouring option descriptions (`--skip`, `--no-autodiscover`, `--context-only`, the `configure` description) were all reworded in this same diff, so these two were simply overlooked.
- `src/config.ts:317-319` still explains that "Reviewers ship as Copilot CLI agents in the plugin's agents/ folder" — the folder this PR deletes.
- The comment newly added at src/commands/configure.ts:35-36 claims "every skill there runs as a forced pass". Under this PR's own model, `origin === 'forced'` skills are pushed into project *context*, not passes (src/dispatch/pass-select.ts:179-182); they only become passes in the no-packs fallback at pass-select.ts:227.

No pass flagged this because configure.ts and the cli.ts option block drew no findings at all, and each stale statement looks correct in isolation — the contradiction is only visible against the example yaml and pass-select.

Fix: point the interactive prompt at `extra_skills_dirs` (keep reading the old key so existing configs migrate), drop or relabel `--reviewer`/`--reviewers-dir` as skill inputs, and correct the two comments (configure.ts:35-36 and config.ts:317-319).
